title: [gateway-core][P1] ferrogate-test ci is red: cancelling an agent job no longer produces a cancel_run dispatch (#502 rework changed the contract)

body:
Owner directive, 2026-07-27: *"因为系统的复杂度上去了,可能不再适合 Caddy 的兼容配置了。需要很强的扩展性的配置文件做法,所以弃用 Caddy 的配置,改为自研的 YAML 主配置文件。"*

## What is actually in the tree today (verified, not assumed)

This is **not** a format port. Three facts change the shape of the work:

1. **YAML already parses.** `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/config/loader.rs:385-395` dispatches on file extension — `yaml`/`yml` → `serde_yaml`, everything else → `toml`. `serde_yaml` is already a workspace dependency and is already used by `ferrogate-auth/src/rbac.rs`. So "support YAML" is done; what is missing is making it **the** format and retiring the alternatives.
2. **The Caddyfile is a third, structurally different path.** `crates/ferrogate-config/src/caddyfile/` is **1263 lines** of hand-written lexer + parser + support, with its own test suite (`caddyfile/parser_tests.rs`, `tests/caddyfile_parser.rs`, `tests/parser_perf.rs`). It does not deserialize into `Config` — it produces a `GatewayConfig` intermediate model that `Config::from_gateway_config` (`loader.rs:115`) then maps. **That mapping layer is the real cost of keeping it, and the real prize for removing it:** every new config capability has to be expressible in a Caddyfile, mapped through the intermediate model, or deliberately excluded — and nothing today records which capabilities took the third option.
3. **The Caddyfile is the default.** `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/cli.rs` has `default_value = "Ferrogate/Caddyfile"` in **three** places. So it is not a legacy compatibility mode a few users opted into; it is what runs when nobody says otherwise.

169 `caddy` references across the Rust tree, in `lifecycle.rs`, `cli.rs`, `responses.rs`, `loader.rs` and the tests.

## Why this is the right call

The extensibility argument is concrete rather than aesthetic. Recent work makes it visible:

- `[tenancy]` (#515) added `implicit_platform_operator` and `require_registered_tenant`, and `[[api_keys]]` grew `platform_operator: Option<bool>` — a **three-state** field whose `null` is meaningful.
- `max_total_gateway_buffer_bytes` + `buffer_admission_wait_ms` (#529) added admission control with an unset-vs-zero distinction that carries different semantics.

Those are ordinary structural config: optional nested records, tri-state flags, unset-vs-explicit-zero. A Caddyfile dialect expresses them badly, and every one of them needs a bespoke line in the mapping layer. That is the extensibility ceiling the directive is describing.

## Scope

1. **Make YAML the primary, documented format**, with a schema designed for FerroGate rather than inherited. Since it is self-designed, decide the shape deliberately — nesting depth, how lists of records read, whether `[[api_keys]]`-style repetition becomes a sequence or a keyed map (a keyed map makes diffs and merges far better, and this config is edited by hand).
2. **Deprecate the Caddyfile path** on a stated timeline: warn on load, then refuse. Change the three `default_value`s. Removing `caddyfile/` deletes 1263 lines and, more valuably, the `from_gateway_config` mapping layer.
3. **Decide TOML's fate explicitly.** It is not the thing being deprecated by the directive, but keeping three formats is worse than keeping two. Recommend: TOML stays parseable for a deprecation window (`_ => toml::from_str` already makes that free) and stops being documented, or is retired alongside — say which, and say when.
4. **Migration tooling is not optional.** `ferrogate config convert <in> <out>` covering Caddyfile→YAML and TOML→YAML, because there are shipped examples (`config/ferrogate.example.toml`, `config/ferrogate.token4ai.example.toml`, `docs/deploy/customer-vpc/{control,data}-plane.toml`) and real deployments.

## The hazard that must be designed in, not discovered

**YAML's implicit typing is a security problem for this particular config**, and it is the one thing TOML was quietly protecting us from:

- `no`, `off`, `n`, `y` parse as booleans in YAML 1.1 — a hostname or region literally called `no` becomes `false`;
- an unquoted `1.20` is a float, `08` may be rejected or read as 8, and a bare `*` is not a string;
- **duplicate keys are not an error by default** — a second `enabled:` silently wins, which in a file that gates authorization is exactly the wrong failure mode.

This config decides tenant isolation and platform-root (#515) and asset admission (#529). A silently coerced value there is a security defect, not a typo. So:

- reject duplicate keys at load, explicitly;
- keep `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` — `TenancyConfig` already has it, and a typo'd key must stay an error, not a silent default;
- have `ferrogate config validate` report the **parsed** value of security-relevant fields, so an operator can see that `region: no` became `false` before it reaches production.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A designed YAML schema is documented, with the shipped examples ported and referenced from the README.
- [ ] Loading a Caddyfile warns and names the migration command; after the stated window it refuses. The three `default_value`s point at the YAML file.
- [ ] `ferrogate config convert` round-trips every shipped example, asserted by a test that loads both forms and compares the resulting `Config` for equality — not the text.
- [ ] Duplicate YAML keys are a load error, with a test.
- [ ] A test pins that the type traps above cannot silently coerce a security-relevant field (`region: no`, `enabled: "false"`, an unquoted `*`).
- [ ] TOML's fate is stated in the docs with a date, whichever way it is decided.
- [ ] `caddyfile/` and `from_gateway_config` are deleted, or an issue tracks their removal with the condition that closes it.

## Note on sequencing

There are ~73 Rust files carrying inline TOML config fixtures and 11 shipped `.toml` files. Those are the bulk of the work and they are mechanical, so this is a good candidate for splitting: the schema + loader + converter first, the fixture migration second. **Do not migrate fixtures before the schema is settled** — that is 73 files rewritten twice.

Refs #515, #529.
title: [config][architecture][P1] Retire the Caddyfile config and make a purpose-built YAML schema the primary config format

body:
Split out of the #502 review (`b67cb40`).

`state_agent_runtime.rs` reclaims a run's dispatch rows on terminal worker
telemetry (`apply_worker_reported_run_state`). At that moment the reporting
worker is by construction the holder of the run's `start_run` lease -- #503's
ownership check just proved it -- and it may not have acked that lease yet.

Consequences:

* `SelfHostedRunAckStatus` has `Completed` / `Failed` / `Cancelled`, so a worker
  that reports `{"state":"completed"}` and THEN acks its lease is a supported
  order. It now gets `InvalidTransport("unknown dispatch")` where it previously
  got 200.
* Any later telemetry for that run fails the #503 ownership check and logs the
  security-shaped "does not hold the lease for" warning instead of the benign
  already-terminal skip.

Not fixed in #502 because the two obvious remedies trade against each other:

* Deferring the delete past the ack window restores the ack, but the majority
  worker never acks at all -- that is exactly the retention leak the reclaim
  exists to close, so the row would survive for the life of the deployment.
* Making the ack tolerate a reclaimed row restores the 200 but there is no
  lease left to prove ownership against, so an authenticated worker in the
  tenant would get a (side-effect-free) 200 on any settled run.

Constraint for the fix: the ack must resolve for the worker that reported the
completion, WITHOUT leaving a permanent row for the never-acking worker. That
most likely means bounding the deferral by the lease expiry, which is the same
sweeper #545 already needs.

Nothing covers this today: both acking tests (`agent_jobs_test.rs`,
`agent_schedule_e2e.rs`) ack `accepted` right after the lease and never report
telemetry.
title: Settling a run deletes the start dispatch its holder has not acked yet

body:
Owner requirement, 2026-07-27: *"任何的动作 API 调用都要带上客户端的 timestamp 和指纹信息,还有 action_id — 这样就知道这个 CLI 何时何地做了什么操作,方便问题追踪和安全审计。"*

## Why this is the missing half, not a new idea

#505 built the **response** side: `MutationReceipt` renders actor, target fingerprint, decision, dry-run and audit id for every mutating verb, and its registry makes "mutating verb returns a bare body" a compile error.

While closing #505 the enumeration found the hard part: of **135 mutating operations in the contract, 117 registry-covered, not one returns an audit identifier.** So the receipt honestly reports `audit_id: null` with `endpoint_returns_no_audit_id` on every mutation. The CLI cannot surface a correlation handle because nothing gives it one.

**This issue is the other end: the CLI mints the handle and sends it.** That is what makes the two sides join up — a client-generated `action_id` on the request is correlatable without waiting for a server-side audit-write path, which #505 declared an explicit non-goal.

## Existing machinery to reuse, not re-invent

- `crates/ferrogate-runtime/src/action_identity.rs` — `ActionIdentity { action, canonical_target, principal, context, fingerprint }` with the `canonical_target_sha256` contract (`"sha256:<hex>"`), from #303/#304.
- `ferrogate-cli-core`'s `MutationReceipt` already carries `action_fingerprint` and asserts byte-equality with `CanonicalCapabilityTarget::fingerprint`. **Do not mint a second fingerprint format** — that assertion exists precisely to stop a CLI-local one appearing.
- `correlation.request_id` / `trace_id` already exist on the receipt.

## Scope

**1. `action_id`** — minted client-side per invocation, sent on every API call (reads too, not only mutations: a read is also "what this CLI did"). Stable across retries of the same logical action, distinct per action.

Decide and document its relationship to the existing **idempotency key**, which is threaded on some resources (`billing`, `agent submit`) and absent on others. They are not the same thing — an idempotency key says "this is the same request, do not repeat the effect"; an action id says "this is the same operator action, here is its thread". Conflating them will hurt later.

**2. Client timestamp** — the moment the CLI issued the call.

> **The trust boundary must be explicit.** A client clock is attacker-controlled and can be skewed by accident. The client timestamp is **evidence about the client**, never an input to an authorization or ordering decision; the server timestamp stays authoritative. Say so in the code and the docs, and make it structurally hard to misuse — e.g. name the field `client_sent_at`, not `timestamp`, so nothing downstream mistakes it for the event time.

**3. Client fingerprint** — what identifies *where* the action came from. Decide the exact field set and justify it. Candidates: CLI version, OS/arch, hostname, the resolved context/profile name, the credential id in use (never the secret).

> **This is the field with a privacy and blast-radius cost.** A hostname or username is PII in some deployments, and it reaches the audit log of a multi-tenant control plane. Decide deliberately: what is collected, whether any of it is hashed rather than sent verbatim, whether an operator can opt out, and what an opt-out does to the audit guarantee. Record the answer on this issue when it closes.

**4. Transport** — headers vs body. Headers keep it uniform across every verb including GETs and avoid touching 135 request schemas; a body field is easier to persist server-side. Pick one and say why. Either way the OpenAPI contract and the generated admin-console client both have gates that will need it declared (`scripts/check-openapi.py`, and the `api-contract-drift` workflow — four issues have been bounced this week for missing the regeneration).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every CLI-issued request carries `action_id`, client timestamp and client fingerprint — enforced **structurally at the single transport chokepoint**, not per command, so a new verb cannot omit them. `ferrogate-cli-core`'s `RenderGate` is the precedent for what "cannot omit" should mean here: a compile error, not a lint.
- [ ] A test enumerates the command registry and fails if any verb can issue a request without them.
- [ ] The client timestamp is named and documented so it cannot be mistaken for the authoritative event time, and no authorization or ordering path reads it — asserted, not left to convention.
- [ ] The `action_id` appears in the `MutationReceipt`, so an operator can correlate what they sent with what came back, and it survives a retry of the same logical action.
- [ ] The fingerprint field set, the hashing decision and the opt-out story are recorded on this issue on close.
- [ ] **No secret material is ever part of the fingerprint** — a test asserts the rendered fingerprint contains no credential, in both `Debug` and serialized form. This repo has an active defect class here (#489, #492, #537), and for a `Vec<u8>` field a plaintext-only assertion is vacuous because a derived `Debug` prints decimal bytes.

## Explicit non-goal

Server-side persistence of these fields. That is the same boundary #505 drew: this issue makes the CLI *send* correlatable identity. Whether the control plane stores it — and the audit-write path that would need — is separate work, and the 135-operation gap above is the evidence it is a real project rather than a small addition.

Refs #505, #303, #304, #358.


---

## Owner clarification, 2026-07-27

> 客户端 CLI 在发起请求携带信息应该包含 **action_id、timestamp、操作系统环境信息、IP 地址**等等,用于**安全审计**。
> 时间戳可以**从服务端获取,然后客户端携带** — 这样就能保证时间安全。

### The server-issued timestamp is the right call, and it changes the design

This removes the trust problem the section above flags, rather than documenting around it. Adopt it: **the CLI does not read its own clock for the audit field.** It obtains the time from the server and echoes it back.

Two things follow, and they should be designed in from the start rather than discovered:

**1. The guarantee is narrower than "when the client acted".** A server-issued token proves *when the server issued it*, not when the operator ran the command. So it must be **short-lived and bound**, otherwise an attacker pre-fetches tokens and replays them later to backdate an action:
- short TTL (seconds, not minutes), rejected outside the window;
- **bound to the `action_id`** it was issued for, so a token cannot be moved onto a different action;
- the server records **its own receive time** alongside it. The issued time and the receive time together bound the action; either alone can be gamed or delayed.

**2. It costs a round trip** unless the token is fetched once and reused — and reuse is exactly what the TTL forbids. Decide explicitly: piggy-back the next token on every response (so the steady state is zero extra round trips and only the first call pays), or accept a `POST /v1/audit/time-token` before each action. The piggy-back design is strongly preferred and should be evaluated first.

### IP address — the client must not be the authority

The client generally cannot know its own public IP, and anything it reports is self-asserted and trivially forged. **The server already observes the source IP; that is the trustworthy record.**

So: the server-observed IP is the authoritative field. A client-reported address may be carried as *additional* evidence — the local interface, the address behind a NAT or proxy, which is genuinely useful for tracing inside a corporate network — but it must be **stored and rendered as client-asserted**, never merged into the authoritative one. Recording a self-reported IP as fact in a security-audit trail is a false record, which is worse than an absent one.

### Field set, consolidated

| field | source | authority |
|---|---|---|
| `action_id` | client-minted | client (it is an identifier, not a claim) |
| `client_sent_at` | **server-issued token, echoed** | server |
| server receive time | server | server |
| OS / arch / CLI version | client | client-asserted |
| hostname, context/profile name | client | client-asserted, PII decision required (see above) |
| credential id in use | client | verifiable against the credential the request authenticated with |
| source IP | **server-observed** | server |
| client-reported IP | client | client-asserted, stored separately |

### Extra acceptance from this clarification

- [ ] The CLI never reads the local clock for the audit timestamp — asserted, not left to convention (a test that fails if `SystemTime::now()` reaches that field).
- [ ] A time token outside its TTL, or presented with a different `action_id` than it was issued for, is refused.
- [ ] Server-observed IP and client-reported IP are distinct fields and are never merged; the rendering says which is which.
- [ ] The steady-state round-trip cost is documented and measured, whichever transport is chosen.
title: [cli][security][P1] Every CLI API call must carry a client timestamp, client fingerprint and action_id, so an operator action is attributable to when and where it was made

body:
Split out of #530, which has carried this as a non-blocking finding for four review rounds. Filing it so it stops being re-derived by the reviewer and starts being owned.

## Problem

`bindSiteDomain`'s 200 is described in `docs/openapi/admin-api.openapi.json` as:

> Existing proven binding for the hostname updated (**re-bound within the same tenant**). Still serving.

The handler does not check tenancy when choosing that status. `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/site_domains.rs:532` passes `existing.is_some()` to the terminal selector, and `existing` is not tenant-filtered. Ownership is the *separate* `holds_binding` test at `:482-484`, and when it is false the upsert is skipped at `:495-508` — while `:536-541` still serializes an `AdminSiteDomainResponse` carrying a `domain` that was never persisted.

## Reachable sequence

1. Tenant B holds an **unproven** claim on `app.example.com`. Because `holder_proven == false` at `:424`, the bind is not refused with 409.
2. Tenant A binds the same hostname with a live ownership proof of its own → `proven == true`, `existing.is_some() == true` → **200**.
3. `holds_binding == false`, so nothing is written.
4. A is told the binding was "re-bound within the same tenant" and is "still serving". Neither is true: it is B's row, and A's claim was not persisted.

The same argument applies one status down: **202**'s "Binding recorded but NOT serving" is also false when `holds_binding` is false, since only the proof row is written.

## Why it matters

#530 exists because a 2xx meant something other than what a client assumes. This is the same defect one layer in: the status code is now correctly *declared*, and the sentence describing it is still wrong. A client that trusts the description will report a successful re-bind to an operator whose domain did not move.

## Ask

- [ ] Decide what a bind by a non-holder against an unproven incumbent should mean, and make the status say it. Either a distinct terminal (e.g. 202 with a "claim recorded, another tenant holds the binding" description), or a refusal — but not a 200 that claims a re-bind that did not happen.
- [ ] Whatever is chosen, the response body must not serialize a `domain` that was never persisted. Returning the *incumbent's* row would be a cross-tenant disclosure; returning A's un-persisted claim is a fabrication. Pick one and record why.
- [ ] Correct the 200 and 202 descriptions in `docs/openapi/admin-api.openapi.json` to match, and regenerate `admin-console/src/lib/api-types.generated.ts` **in the same commit** (a sibling was bounced for landing generator output separately).

## Verification

- [ ] A test that drives the sequence above — B holds an unproven claim, A binds with a live proof — and asserts the terminal and the body by identity, not just the status class.
- [ ] State the mutation that reds it. Per #500, a green suite is not evidence on its own.
- [ ] Note that `site_domain_bind_status` is sealed inside `mod bind_terminal` (`site_domains.rs:1084-1108`) as of #530; a new terminal goes through the selector, and `every_bind_terminal_is_declared_in_the_openapi_document` will force the spec edit.

## Notes

`existing.is_some()` vs `holds_binding` is a two-argument confusion at one call site, so the fix is likely small; the decision about what the status should *mean* is the substantive part.

Filed by the code-review agent at #530's pass, per that review's own recommendation.

body:
Found by the #535 sweep, reported rather than folded in because it is outside that issue's stated scope.

`GET /admin/v1/agent-workflows` and `GET /admin/v1/agent-workflows/{id}` (`crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/local.rs`) serialize `AgentWorkflowPolicy`, which carries the same three id families as the surfaces #518 and #535 closed — `organization_ids`, `project_ids`, `api_key_ids` (`config/types.rs`) — to **any tenant-scoped `admin.read` key**, i.e. the exact shape `provision_gateway_api_key` mints for every admin-console login.

Same `Ok(_) =>` discard-the-`AuthContext` shape. Writes are gated; this is pure disclosure.

## Why this one is cheap

`ConfigCatalogScope` (added for #535 in `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/rbac.rs`) **applies verbatim** — same selector semantics, same narrowing rule. This should be an application of the existing helper, not a new pattern. Follow #535's treatment exactly, including:

- empty selector = wildcard = genuinely global, returned to everyone;
- non-empty selector = allow-list, visible only if it names something the caller owns;
- a policy naming both A and B is visible to A **with B's ids stripped**;
- `narrow()` must return `None` (hide), never an empty vec — an emptied selector re-renders as a wildcard, which reads as "applies to everyone";
- the by-id read must refuse out-of-scope **identically to absent**, and a platform operator must still get **404** for a genuinely absent id (this is the assertion #518 was bounced for missing, and #535 pinned separately from its scope assertions — do the same).

## Worth knowing before you start

**The data plane already scopes workflows per caller** (`gateway/chat.rs`, `gateway/agent_runs.rs`), so only the admin read is unscoped. That means this is a disclosure fix with no data-plane behaviour change, and it also means there is an existing notion of "which workflows this caller may see" to check the new scoping against.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Both reads scoped through `ConfigCatalogScope`; no second pattern introduced.
- [ ] OpenAPI descriptions state the scoping and the by-id refusal contract, client regenerated **in the same commit** (there is a CI gate on that drift).
- [ ] Operator-404 pinned per by-id endpoint, separately from the scope assertions.
- [ ] A test asserts tenant B's ids are absent from tenant A's view **by identity**, not just by substring.

Refs #535, #518.
title: [gateway-core][P2] GET /admin/v1/agent-workflows leaks other tenants' org/project/api-key ids (third sibling of #518/#535)

body:
Split from #502 at the dev agent's own disclosure — the one reclaim hole its fix does not cover.

#502 (`b177027`) makes settlement reclaim a run's `self_hosted_run_dispatches` rows at four points: worker-reported terminalization, ack of a `cancel_run`, cancel of an unleased job, and a retried cancel on an already-terminal job.

**The hole: a job a worker leased and then abandoned.** Its `cancel_run` is never acked and its start dispatch is superseded but not deleted, so **two rows persist** until some caller happens to retry the cancel. The slot is free — the run is terminal — so a tenant with a lease-and-vanish worker accumulates rows **without ever tripping the cap**, which is precisely the retention pressure #502 was supposed to remove.

## Wanted

A periodic reclaim for dispatches whose run has been terminal for longer than the lease duration, modelled on `sweep_asset_lifecycle_once`.

**The constraint that makes this non-trivial:** it must not delete a `start_run` whose run is still live. #503's lease-ownership proof reads that row for the whole life of the run, so a sweeper that keys only off age will break lease ownership. Terminal-status plus lease-expiry is the condition, not age alone.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A run terminal for longer than the lease duration has its orphaned dispatch rows reclaimed without any caller action.
- [ ] A live run's `start_run` row is never deleted, asserted directly rather than implied — #503's proof must keep working.
- [ ] The sweeper is idempotent and bounded (it runs on a schedule against a table nothing else prunes).
- [ ] A test drives lease-then-abandon and asserts the rows are gone afterwards, and a sibling asserts a live run survives the same sweep.

Refs #502, #503.
title: [gateway-core][P3] Reclaim dispatch rows for runs that settled but were never acknowledged

body:
## Problem

`cargo test -p ferrogate-cli` is red on `main` (`0052ec0`): 1352 passed, **1 failed**,
deterministically (3/3 runs).

```
thread 'gateway::asset_admission::asset_admission_test::a_queued_large_read_is_not_barged_by_a_later_small_one'
panicked at crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/asset_admission_test.rs:346:5:
assertion `left == right` failed: the queued read must still be waiting, with half
the budget free -- otherwise this proves nothing about barging
  left: 0
 right: 4194304
```

The failing test is one `0052ec0` — *(#529) Make the aggregate ceiling true on the
two surfaces that only claimed it* — introduced itself, so the slice landed red.

Note what the assertion message says about itself: *"otherwise this proves nothing
about barging"*. The author wrote a precondition check precisely so the test could
not pass vacuously, and that precondition is what is failing — so the barging
property is currently **unproven**, not merely untested. Either the admission
budget is not being released the way the test expects, or the test's setup no
longer establishes the state it needs. Both readings need the same investigation.

Found by the test gate while gating #515 (unrelated).

## Reproduce

```
cargo test -j4 -p ferrogate-cli --locked --bins a_queued_large_read_is_not_barged_by_a_later_small_one
```

Fails 3/3. Use `-j4`, not `-j8` — `-j8` OOM-kills this box.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `cargo test -p ferrogate-cli` is green on `main`.
- [ ] The fix identifies which side was wrong — the budget accounting or the test's setup — and says so; do not adjust the expected number until that is answered.
- [ ] The barging property is mutation-verified: allowing a later small read to jump the queued large one must turn this test red. A precondition that no longer holds means the test proved nothing, which is the failure mode #500 is about.

## Related

Two other slices landed red on `main` this session and were caught the same way:
#538 (from #515, since fixed) and #541 (from #529, the workspace clippy sweep).
This is the third from the same window — `cargo test -p ferrogate-cli` is not
being run before push. See #531 for the frontend equivalent.


---

## Acceptance amendment, 2026-07-27 (recorded by the code-review agent at pass)

**Box 3 — "The barging property is mutation-verified: allowing a later small read to jump the queued large one must turn this test red" — is retired, not delivered.**

`cf9885b` took resolution option 2 of the review's three: the anti-barging property is **tokio's**, not FerroGate's. `poll_acquire` (`batch_semaphore.rs:426-432`) takes all available permits and CASes the counter to `0` when it must queue for the remainder; `add_permits_locked` (`:310-333`) assigns releases head-first and only returns surplus to the counter inside `if rem > 0 && is_empty` (`:342`), observed under the waitlist lock. Free capacity and a queued waiter are therefore mutually exclusive, so the `waiting` guard #529 added was redundant — and it has been deleted along with its counter.

There is consequently **no product branch left to mutate**, which is why the box cannot be ticked as written. The observable property (a queued large read is eventually served; an over-budget read sheds after the bounded wait) is pinned by `a_queued_large_read_is_not_barged_by_a_later_small_one` and `an_over_budget_read_is_shed_after_the_bounded_wait_not_queued_forever`.

The confirming run belongs to the test gate: **re-add the guard and confirm the suite stays green.** If it reds, the redundancy reading is wrong and the deletion must be reverted.

title: [gateway-core][P1] main is red: a_queued_large_read_is_not_barged_by_a_later_small_one fails deterministically (#529 landed with its own test failing)

body:
## Problem

`rbac_catalog_scope` (`crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/rbac.rs:1107-1130`) makes
a security claim in its own doc comment that nothing holds:

> *"Storage failures propagate rather than degrading to an empty (or, **far worse, unfiltered**) scope: the callers turn them into the same `503 storage_unavailable` they already return for a failed list."*

The code is correct today — both storage calls use `?`. But the fail-closed
property is untested, so it can be inverted with every suite still green.

**Mutation, run by the test gate while gating #518:**

```rust
// instead of `state.list_tenant_role_bindings(tenant_id).await?`
let Ok(bindings) = state.list_tenant_role_bindings(tenant_id).await else {
    return Ok(RbacCatalogScope::Full);   // degrade to the UNFILTERED catalog
};
```

```
cargo test -p ferrogate-cli --test rbac_catalog_scope_admin_api
    -> test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed
```

All five #518 tests stay green while a storage blip hands every tenant-scoped
caller the entire platform RBAC catalog — precisely the disclosure #518 was filed
to close, reachable again through the error path.

For contrast, the two properties that *are* held died immediately under mutation:
discarding the `AuthContext` reds all 5, and turning the by-id GET back into an
existence oracle reds exactly the one test that owns it. This is the third
property, and it is the only unheld one.

## Why it is a separate issue

#518's stated ask ("add a test that goes red when the `AuthContext` is discarded
again") is met and mutation-proven, so #518 passed the gate. This is a narrower,
distinct claim on the error path, and closing it needs infrastructure that does
not exist yet: there is **no** storage fault-injection anywhere in the repo
(`grep -rn 'fail_next|inject_failure|FaultyStore|force_error' crates/` → no hits)
and **no** test anywhere asserts `storage_unavailable`. That is real work, not an
omission to bolt onto #518.

## Ask

- Add a way to make a storage read fail on demand for the admin surfaces — a test-only failing `AppState` store, or a `#[cfg(test)]` fault hook on the list calls.
- Pin that a storage failure inside `rbac_catalog_scope` yields `503 storage_unavailable`, never a `Full` scope and never a silently empty one.
- **Verify by inverting**: the mutation above must turn the new test red. A test that passes against `return Ok(RbacCatalogScope::Full)` has not held anything (#500).

body:
Surfaced while root-causing #538. **Pre-existing, not introduced by #515** — but #515's new test is the first thing in the repo that touches it.

## The defect

`crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4777`:

```rust
pub(crate) fn auth_required(&self) -> bool {
    self.config.auth_service.enabled || !self.config.api_keys.is_empty()
}
```

It counts **static config keys only**. Durable/virtual keys — the ones minted through `POST /admin/v1/virtual-keys` and stored in the control plane — do not make authentication required.

`authenticate_with_admission` opens with:

```rust
if !state.auth_required() {
    return Ok(AuthContext { scopes: {WILDCARD}, platform_operator: true, organization_id: None, ... });
}
```

So for a deployment configured with **no `[[api_keys]]` block and no external auth service**, but with virtual keys in storage:

- every request is admitted **without presenting any credential at all**;
- the resulting context carries the wildcard scope and, since #515 made it explicit, `platform_operator: true` — i.e. platform root;
- the durable authenticator is never consulted, so a presented virtual key is neither validated nor attributed.

That is the whole tenancy model bypassed by an empty config section.

## Why it went unnoticed

Every durable-key test in `auth_test.rs` carries `api_keys: vec![decoy_yaml_key()]` **precisely so `auth_required()` is true** — the decoy exists to switch authentication on, not to be authenticated against. The one test that omitted it (#515's `durable_virtual_key_is_never_platform_root`) went red immediately, which is how this was found. So the fixture convention has been silently compensating for the gap.

Before #515 the zero-config context had `organization_id: None`, which every isolation check *already* read as platform root — so the behaviour is unchanged, and #515 only made it legible by writing the field down.

## Severity, stated honestly

Whether this is reachable in a real deployment depends on whether anyone runs with an empty `api_keys` and storage-backed keys only. That is a plausible managed/multi-tenant posture — mint keys through the admin API, keep none in the file — and it is exactly the posture the virtual-key feature exists to serve. It should be confirmed against a real config before assigning an exploit narrative, which is why this says P1 rather than P0.

## Ask

1. Decide what makes authentication required. Candidate: `auth_service.enabled || !api_keys.is_empty() || <the control plane has any active virtual key>` — but a storage read on every request is not acceptable, so it likely needs a startup-resolved flag plus an explicit config switch.
2. Whatever the rule, make the **zero-config wildcard posture something an operator opts into by name** (`[auth] disabled = true` or similar), not the value an empty section lands on. This is the same shape as #515/#540: an omission must not silently grant root.
3. A test that boots with **no** static keys, a virtual key in storage, and asserts an unauthenticated request is refused.
4. Check the sibling: `check_network_access` and any other pre-auth gate that keys off the same predicate.

Refs #538, #515, #540.
title: [gateway-core][security][P1] auth_required() ignores durable/virtual keys — a deployment whose only credentials live in storage has authentication switched off

body:
## Problem

`cargo +1.88.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings`
exits **101** on `main` (`e18204a`). The complete failure set is one lint:

```
error: unnecessary map of the identity function
  --> crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/asset_admission_test.rs:130:15
```

```rust
let refusal = budget
    .admit(8 * MIB)
    .await
    .map_err(|refusal| refusal)   // <-- identity
    .err()
    .expect("the second read must be shed, not admitted and not hung");
```

`.map_err(|refusal| refusal)` is a no-op — it maps the error to itself, then the
next line takes `.err()` anyway. Deleting the line is behaviour-preserving.

Introduced by `b2f6e2d` — *(#529) Bound the aggregate, not just the per-operation,
asset read buffer* — which landed **after** #513 (`df8ebea`) had cleared the last
two lints, so it reopened the gate #513 exists to hold shut. Found by the test
gate while gating #513; #513's own fix is intact and mutation-verified, and
`ferrogate-storage` is clean.

## Reproduce

```
cargo +1.88.0 clippy -j4 --workspace --all-targets --keep-going --locked -- -D warnings
```

`--keep-going` matters: the plain sweep aborts at the first failing crate and
under-reports. This run went to completion, so the one lint above is the whole
remaining set. Use `-j4`, not `-j8` — `-j8` OOM-kills this box.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `cargo +1.88.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings` exits 0.
- [ ] The identity `map_err` is removed rather than `#[allow]`-ed — there is no behaviour to preserve.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ferrogate-cli` still covers the shed path the assertion is about (the test must still fail if `admit` starts admitting the second read).

body:
Split from #515, at the code-review agent's direction. #515 delivered stage 1 — the *mechanism* for declaring platform root — but deliberately left the default permissive. This issue is the flip, and it is the half that actually closes #515's non-negotiable:

> `organization_id: None` meaning "platform root" must become explicit opt-in, not the default an omitted config field lands on.

Today, out of the box, an omitted field still grants platform root byte-for-byte as before, and #515's own probe (`GET /admin/v1/tenant-roles/tenant-b` → 200 from an unscoped key) still reproduces.

## What stage 1 already built (do not redo)

- `ApiKey::platform_operator: Option<bool>` — explicit opt-in — and a `[tenancy]` config section.
- `CallerScope { PlatformOperator, Tenant(&str) }` with `resolve_platform_operator()` as the single classification chokepoint all three auth sources run.
- `finalize_auth` refuses an unclassifiable credential with `403 tenant_identity_required`.
- `platform_operator = true` **plus** `organization_id` is a load-time error and a 400 on the admin write path.
- `Config::validate` names every key relying on implicit root at startup, by id, with the exact fix — this is the migration window's only user-visible artifact.

## The flip

- [ ] `TenancyConfig::default()` → `implicit_platform_operator: false` (`config/types.rs`).
- [ ] `config/loader.rs` — env-derived keys stop landing on `organization_id: None, platform_operator: None`; decide whether the bootstrap key declares `platform_operator = true` explicitly or the loader fails closed with a named error.
- [ ] Annotate the in-tree config fixtures. **This is the bulk of the work: ~270 of them**, plus `config/ferrogate.example.toml` and `docs/deploy/customer-vpc/control-plane.toml`, which stage 1 already updated as the demonstration.
- [ ] Decide `require_registered_tenant`'s default in the same pass — it is the sibling switch and flipping one without the other leaves a half-migrated posture.

## Why it was staged, and what could go wrong

A fail-closed default was rejected in stage 1 for a concrete reason: ~270 in-tree fixtures plus real env-derived bootstrap keys are root today. Flipping silently breaks the data plane; erroring at load breaks every one of them on upgrade. Stage 1 therefore keeps the legacy answer and shouts about it at startup.

**The risk this issue carries is that the flip is done mechanically and locks someone out of their own control plane.** The guard against that is `tenancy_config_defaults_are_legacy_compatible_and_explicit`, which exists specifically so stage 2 cannot happen *by accident* — expect to change that test deliberately, and treat needing to change it as the signal that you are doing stage 2 rather than a refactor.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A config that declares no identity for a key fails closed — refused at authentication or at load, not silently granted root.
- [ ] `GET /admin/v1/tenant-roles/{other-tenant}` from an unscoped key no longer answers 200 (#515's original probe).
- [ ] Every in-tree fixture and shipped example is annotated, so `cargo test` and the harness run under the new default.
- [ ] The deprecation note on `implicit_platform_operator` is removed or the switch deleted outright.

Refs #515, #340.
title: [gateway-core][P1] Stage 2 of #515: flip the tenancy defaults so an omitted organization_id no longer grants platform root

`docs/cloudflare-deploy-topology.md` §8 enumerates six follow-up issues and says explicitly that it deliberately did not create them. None was ever filed, so every *"pending verification"* note in that document — and the §6 "bindings beat REST" recommendation those notes back — has no tracked owner.

Filed as **one tracking issue rather than six board items**, deliberately: the board carries 31 Backlog items and the repo is under a "finish core + CLI first" directive, so six new Cloudflare items would be noise that outranks nothing. If a reviewer prefers six separate issues, say so and I will split it — the point is that the work is tracked, not the shape.

## 1. Execute the §9 Containers PoC runbook — the one that unblocks the rest

Run §9 on a live Cloudflare account and record: image boots, `/healthz` + `/readyz` against external Postgres (**the unconfirmed 5432-egress question**), one proxied `/v1/chat/completions`, cold-start numbers, DO-duration billing on a streamed response, and shim latency. Then update the document's "pending verification" notes with measured values.

This is the empirical basis the §8 recommendation rests on. Until it runs, §6's decision is reasoned, not measured. Note it **cannot be done in the dev environment** — there is no live Cloudflare account and no network here.

- [ ] P1–P8 executed on a live account
- [ ] 5432 egress result recorded (this is the go/no-go for external Postgres)
- [ ] DO-duration billing measured on a streamed response
- [ ] `docs/cloudflare-deploy-topology.md` "pending verification" notes replaced with measurements

## The remaining five

- [ ] **2. Edge Worker for the hybrid topology** — thin auth/cache/guardrail pre-check Worker forwarding to the FerroGate origin; per-route rollout config. This is Phase 1 of §8 and the only phase marked "now".
- [ ] **3. On-CF config profile** — documented preset: `listen = "0.0.0.0:8080"`, TLS/ACME disabled, readiness tuned for `startAndWaitForPorts`, sweeper behaviour under restart documented. Note §3's finding that the sweepers assume a continuously-running process, so a scale-to-zero topology silently pauses them — that belongs in this preset's documentation.
- [ ] **4. Rust binding-shim client** — small module speaking plain HTTP to the `outboundByHost` virtual hosts; integrate with the `cf://` resolver seam (#423/#417) and `AgentMemoryClient` (#427); REST fallback preserved off-CF.
- [ ] **5. Containers deploy pipeline** — extend the #413 Worker deploy pipeline with `wrangler deploy` of the container app + image push; CI image build for `linux/amd64`.
- [ ] **6. D1 control-plane backend spike** — validate the Cloudflare D1 route against RuntimeControlPlaneBackend and the repository traits delivered by #419/#420; record which repository surfaces can run through D1 without weakening atomicity, migration, or durability contracts.

## Ordering

Item 1 gates items 3–5 (they encode decisions the PoC has not yet validated). Item 2 is independent and is the phase §8 recommends doing now.

Refs #424, #484.

body:
## Problem

`cargo test -p ferrogate-cli` is red on `main` (`1f08dff`): **1336 passed, 2 failed**.
Both failures were introduced by `c597ddf` — *(#515) Make `organization_id` a
declared tenant identity, and platform root an opt-in* — which is the newest of
the three auth-touching commits on main (`c597ddf` newer than `73dfbc4`/`4d5fcce`
from #517). Both are tests **#515 added itself**, so the slice landed red rather
than being broken by something downstream.

Found by the test gate while gating #493 (unrelated — the Cloudflare error mapper).

### 1. `auth::auth_test::durable_virtual_key_is_never_platform_root` — the security claim does not hold

```
panicked at crates/ferrogate-cli/src/auth_test.rs:1488:5:
assertion failed: !auth.is_platform_operator()
```

The test (`auth_test.rs:1477-1490`) is #515's own statement of the invariant its
commit message promises:

```rust
config.tenancy.implicit_platform_operator = true;
seed_durable_virtual_key(&state, "vk-515", secret, |_| {});
let auth = authenticate(&state, &bearer_headers(secret), "chat.completions", "req-1")...;
assert!(!auth.is_platform_operator());              // <-- fails
assert_eq!(auth.caller_scope(), CallerScope::Tenant("tenant-1"));
```

Its own doc comment states the contract: *"A durable/virtual key is minted under
a tenant, so it is tenant-scoped no matter what the compatibility switch says:
the storage path can never produce a platform-root credential."*

As shipped, it can. With `tenancy.implicit_platform_operator = true`, a
**tenant-scoped durable virtual key authenticates as a platform operator** — a
privilege-escalation shape, and precisely the case the compatibility switch was
supposed to stop being able to reach. Whether the defect is in the storage
authentication path or in the switch's precedence needs root-causing; the test
is asserting the right thing.

### 2. `gateway::governed_decision::governed_decision_test::scanner_finds_no_governed_code_outside_the_vocabulary`

```
these governed error codes are emitted by the proxy but have no entry in
GOVERNED_ERROR_VOCABULARY: ["tenant_identity_required"]. Add one, declaring the
stage it is produced at and whether a conformance fixture is required.
```

#515 emits `tenant_identity_required` at `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/auth.rs:825`
without registering it. The scanner test is doing exactly its job — this one is a
straightforward missing declaration.

## Reproduce

```
cargo test -j4 -p ferrogate-cli --locked
```

(`-j4`, not `-j8` — `-j8` OOM-kills this box.)

## Acceptance

- [ ] `cargo test -p ferrogate-cli` is green on `main`.
- [ ] Finding 1 is fixed at the authentication path, not by relaxing the assertion or by deleting the test — a durable/virtual key must stay `CallerScope::Tenant` with `implicit_platform_operator = true`.
- [ ] Mutation-verify finding 1: re-introducing the promotion must turn `durable_virtual_key_is_never_platform_root` red. A fix whose test still passes against the broken code is not a fix (see #500).
- [ ] `tenant_identity_required` has a `GOVERNED_ERROR_VOCABULARY` entry declaring its stage and whether a conformance fixture is required.

body:
Found while verifying #492, whose three enumerated types are already fixed (`e539914`). These four are the same defect class and were outside that issue's explicit scope, so they were left alone rather than silently widened.

A derived `Debug` over a struct holding plaintext credential material means the secret can reach a log line, an `anyhow` error chain, a panic message, or a test-failure dump, from any `{:?}` anywhere — including code that never intended to touch the secret.

## The four

1. **`crates/ferrogate-auth/src/admin_console.rs:167` — `AdminSessionResponse`. The strongest candidate.** It derives `Debug` over **three** credentials at once: `access_token`, `refresh_token`, and `gateway_api_key`. It is the login/refresh reply, and `gateway_api_key` is the **once-shown minted key** from #517 — structurally the closest analogue to the minted R2 credential that #489 removed a derive for, and still unguarded.
2. `crates/ferrogate-auth/src/admin_console.rs:143` — `AdminRefreshRequest.refresh_token`, derived `Debug`, parsed from a request body exactly like the login payload #492 fixed.
3. `crates/ferrogate-auth/src/admin_console.rs:148` — `AdminLogoutRequest.refresh_token`, same.
4. `crates/ferrogate-auth/src/rbac.rs:55` — `AuthApiKey.secret: Option<String>`, derived `Debug` over an API key secret.

## Fix

Same precedent as #489/#492: drop the derive, hand-write `Debug` printing the non-secret fields plus `<redacted>` (or a length, as `AdminScimTokenResponse` does with `token_len`), and document why.

**Two traps carried forward:**

- **The #489 vacuity trap** — a test asserting only that the rendered string lacks the plaintext can be vacuous for non-`String` fields, because a derived `Debug` over `Vec<u8>` prints decimal bytes. These four are all `String`/`Option<String>`, so a plaintext assertion does bite — but assert the positive shape too, so an impl that *drops* the field instead of redacting is not silently accepted. #492's tests are the model: they check secret-body substrings, prefixes at 4/8/16 chars, and that the surviving non-secret fields are still printed.
- **`Option<String>`** (case 4) needs the `Some`/`None` distinction preserved without leaking the value — `Some("<redacted>")` vs `None`, not a flattened `<redacted>` for both.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each of the four types has a hand-written `Debug` that cannot emit the secret; `AdminSessionResponse` redacts all three of its credential fields.
- [ ] A regression test per type, asserting both the absence of the secret (and its prefixes) and the presence of the non-secret shape.
- [ ] `Clone`/`PartialEq`/`Serialize`/`Deserialize` untouched, so wire formats and equality are unchanged — verify no call site depended on the old `Debug` output.

## Note for whoever picks this up

`crates/ferrogate-auth/src/admin_console.rs` sees frequent traffic (#517 landed there recently). Check for a live agent in that file before starting.

Refs #492, #489, #517.
title: [security][P2] Four more derived Debug impls print plaintext credentials — session tokens, refresh tokens, and the once-shown gateway API key

body:
Split out of #488's code-review bounce (finding 3) so the security mechanism can advance on its own. #488's gate itself was reviewed as clean; this is its missing operator surface.

## Problem

After #488, `POST /admin/v1/site-domains` answers **202** for every bind whose ownership is not already proven: the binding is recorded, the hostname is deliberately kept OUT of the ACME order set, and it will not serve until `POST /admin/v1/site-domains/{hostname}/verify` succeeds.

`admin-console/src/pages/site-domains.tsx:74-96` does not model that state:

- `gateway-client.ts:236` treats 202 as `response.ok`, so `onSuccess` fires and toasts `toast.bound` — the operator is told the domain is bound.
- The page never reads `verification` / `challenge_record_value` / `verification_state`, so **the TXT record the operator must publish is never displayed**.
- There is no affordance to call `verifySiteDomain` afterwards.

Net effect: an operator binds a domain from the console, is told it worked, and the domain never serves — with the one piece of information needed to fix it (the challenge value) returned by the API and discarded by the UI.

## What is already in place

- The API returns everything needed: `verification.state`, the challenge record name and value, and `site_domain.serving`.
- **`202` is now declared in the OpenAPI contract** with a description telling clients to branch on `site_domain.serving` rather than infer from the status code (#530, `ff80447`).
- **The generated client is regenerated** and carries `verifySiteDomain`, `AdminSiteDomainVerification` and `verification_state` (#488, `28fabd2`), so the types exist — this is UI work only.

## Scope

- Treat 202 as its own outcome in the bind flow, not as success.
- Render the challenge record name + value with a copy affordance, and the current `verification_state`.
- Add the verify action, and reflect `serving` in the domain list so "bound" and "serving" are visually distinct.
- Cover it with a component test, and a Playwright flow if the page already has one.

## Priority note

Filed at P2 and deliberately **not** picked up now: the repo is under a "finish core + CLI first, admin-console last" directive. This is console feature work, not a gate-unblocker, so it waits. The security gap #488 fixes is closed regardless — this issue is about the console being able to drive it.

Refs #488, #530.
title: [admin-console][P2] Site-domain bind page reports success on a 202 and never shows the DNS challenge, so a bind cannot be completed from the console

body:
Found during the adversarial review pass on #518. **Not a regression from `0c0631a`** — these are siblings that #518's fix did not touch. Filing separately so #518 can land on its own scope.

#518 fixed the RBAC catalog (`/admin/v1/permissions`, `/admin/v1/roles`, and both by-id reads). The same `Ok(_) =>` discard-the-`AuthContext` shape survives on two other admin read surfaces, so the class "any tenant-scoped `admin.read` key reads platform-global state" is **not** eliminated.

## Leak 1 — `/admin/v1/policies` (worse of the two)

`crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/local.rs:8589`:

```rust
match authenticate(&state, headers, "admin.read", &ctx.request_id).await {
    Ok(_) => {
        let body = AdminList::new(state.config.policies.clone());
```

`GET /admin/v1/policies` with a tenant-A-scoped `admin.read` key — the exact key shape `provision_gateway_api_key` mints for every admin-console login — returns **200 with every `PolicyRule` verbatim**. `PolicyRule` (`crates/ferrogate-cli/src/config/types.rs:1335-1355`) carries:

- `organization_ids: Vec<String>`
- `project_ids: Vec<String>`
- `api_key_ids: Vec<String>`
- plus `effect`, `models`, `providers`, `code`, `message`

So tenant A learns other tenants' org ids, project ids and API-key ids, and exactly which models/providers are denied to them.

`GET /admin/v1/policies/{name}` (`local.rs:8604-8622`) is the matching unscoped by-id read, and names come free from the list — together they are a full enumeration primitive.

Writes are correctly gated (`require_platform_operator`, `local.rs:8670`), so this is pure disclosure. Payload is non-empty exactly where an operator has configured `[[policies]]` with tenant/key selectors — i.e. the multi-tenant configuration #518 assumes.

## Leak 2 — `/admin/v1/gateway-configs`

`crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/local.rs:859-873`, serializer at `:10083`. Same `Ok(_)` discard. `GET /admin/v1/gateway-configs` with a tenant-scoped `admin.read` key returns every `AdminGatewayConfigProfile` including `api_key_ids` — the static config-key ids attached to each profile, across all tenants. Weaker than leak 1 (ids only, no policy semantics), same shape.

## Ask

- [ ] Decide, per surface, whether it is public-to-tenants by design. If it is, say so in the OpenAPI description so it stops reading as an oversight; if not, scope it.
- [ ] If scoped: filter `/admin/v1/policies` and `/admin/v1/policies/{name}` by the caller's tenant. Reuse #518's pattern — a single helper resolving the caller's scope from `AuthContext`, applied at every read site — rather than open-coding the filter per handler.
- [ ] Same for `/admin/v1/gateway-configs` and its by-id read.
- [ ] Keep the by-id reads from becoming existence oracles: return the same status for out-of-scope and nonexistent, as #518 does at `rbac.rs:124-133`.
- [ ] Sweep for the remaining instances of the shape rather than fixing only these two: `git grep -n 'Ok(_) =>' crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/` against every handler that authenticates with `admin.read` and then serializes platform-global state.

## Verification

- [ ] A test per surface that goes red when the `AuthContext` is discarded again — seed tenant B's rows through an **operator** key, authenticate as tenant A, assert B's rows are absent **by identity**, not by count. (#518's `crates/ferrogate-cli/tests/rbac_catalog_scope_admin_api.rs` is the model; it survives mutation honestly.)
- [ ] State the mutation that reds each new test. Per #500, a green suite is not evidence on its own.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p ferrogate-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `python3 scripts/check-openapi.py`, and — if the spec changes — `cd admin-console && npm run check:api-types` (regenerating the client is required; #518 was bounced for missing exactly this).

## Notes

- Severity is disclosure-only on both: all write paths are operator-gated.
- The RBAC catalog itself is genuinely closed by #518 — I could not substantiate any path back to another tenant's roles or permissions.

Filed by the code-review agent while reviewing #518.

body:
Found while reviewing #527. Not caused by it — #527's diff cannot touch these files — and disclosed accurately by the dev agent rather than absorbed.

## Symptom

`admin-console` unit suite is red on `origin/main` (`0277cf2`):

```
cd admin-console && npm run test -- --run
=> 3 failed | 26 passed
   src/pages/assets.test.tsx  (presigned upload / cancellation)
```

Reproduced independently in a throwaway worktree at `origin/main` with the existing `node_modules`.

## Why this is P1 and not "just three failing tests"

`scripts/check-admin-console.sh` runs `npm run test -- --run` **before** the build step, so the whole admin-console gate is red for everyone, all the time. #527 just landed `src/lib/typecheck.gate.test.ts`, whose entire purpose is to make a typecheck regression fail loudly inside that same run — but a new failure now arrives inside a suite that is *already* failing, which is exactly how a stable red stops being read. #527 exists to kill that dynamic; this issue is the same dynamic one layer out.

## Scope

- [ ] Diagnose the 3 `assets.test.tsx` failures (presigned upload and cancellation paths) and fix the real cause — the product code or the test, whichever is actually wrong. Do not skip, `.skip`, or delete the tests to green the gate.
- [ ] If the tests are wrong, say what the correct behaviour is and pin it; if the product is wrong, the fix belongs in the presigned-upload path, not the assertion.
- [ ] Check the fixtures against the real gateway payload type rather than the hand-written shape — the #343 failure mode (a fixture encoding a shape the gateway does not emit, making both suites green over a broken product) applies directly to presigned-upload responses.

## Verification

- [ ] `cd admin-console && npm run test -- --run` — unpiped; 0 failed.
- [ ] `bash scripts/check-admin-console.sh` — exits 0 end to end (lint, test, typecheck gate, build).
- [ ] For each of the 3 tests, state the mutation that reds it — i.e. break the thing the test names and show the test notices. Per #500, a green suite is not evidence on its own.

## Notes

- `npm run lint` and `npx tsc -b` are both green at `origin/main`; this is unit-test-only.
- There is no GitHub Actions workflow for `admin-console` (`.github/workflows/` is Rust-only, per the repo's no-Actions release directive), so `scripts/check-admin-console.sh` is the gate.

Filed by the code-review agent while reviewing #527.

title: [admin-console][P1] npm run test is red on main — 3 assets.test.tsx failures block the admin-console gate

body:
Found while landing #527 (`tsc -b` red on `main`). Not caused by that slice.

## Problem

Three tests in `admin-console/src/pages/assets.test.tsx` — the presigned large-object upload / cancellation flow — fail on a **clean `main` checkout**.

Verification method: the #527 dev agent `git stash`ed its own changes and re-ran the suite, getting an identical failure set on unmodified `main`. So these are pre-existing and independent of #527's OpenAPI/generated-types change.

## Why file it rather than absorb it

#527's own text makes the argument better than I can:

> A stable, well-understood red is more dangerous than a flaky one, because it stops being read.

This is now the **fifth** instance this session of a check believed to be running/green that is not:

- #499 — `scripts/check-workers.sh` never invoked by CI
- #506 / #509 / #513 — clippy gate red on `main`
- #508 — Node off-`PATH`, admin-console gate silently skipped
- #525 — `security-check.sh` secret scan never runs (no ripgrep)
- **this one** — admin-console vitest red on `main`

#510 is the cautionary precedent: seven vitest failures were waved through as "known pre-existing, unrelated" by several gate runs, and turned out to be a 13-line jsdom polyfill gap that was **masking the acceptance-critical publish-path coverage of an entire issue**. "Pre-existing" is a description, not a diagnosis — nobody has yet established whether these three are an environment gap or genuine broken coverage of the presigned upload path.

## Ask

- Diagnose the three failures. Specifically determine whether they are an **environment/polyfill gap** (the #510 shape) or a **real regression in the presigned upload/cancellation flow**. Do not close as "environment" without showing which API is missing and why the test needs it.
- Fix them, or — if they are asserting something genuinely obsolete — delete them with a stated reason. Do not `skip` them into permanent invisibility.
- Note the interaction with #508: if admin-console deps/Node are absent on the CI box, this suite may not be running there at all, in which case the red is only visible locally and the CI signal is separately wrong.

## Not yet determined

I did not reproduce these myself — the loop's dev box has the #508 problem (Node off-`PATH`, admin-console deps absent), so the evidence here is the #527 agent's stash-and-rerun rather than an independent run. The **first step for whoever picks this up is an independent reproduction**; if the suite passes on a properly provisioned box, that itself is the finding and points at #508.

Refs #527, #510, #508.
title: [admin-console][testing][P2] 3 assets.test.tsx presigned-upload tests are red on main — a fifth 'gate believed green' instance

body:
## Problem

`npx vitest run` in `admin-console` is red on `main` (`e3ed951`, node v24.18.0):

```
Test Files  1 failed | 84 passed (85)
     Tests  3 failed | 614 passed (617)

FAIL src/pages/assets.test.tsx > presigned large-object upload > runs register-intent -> direct PUT -> commit in order with verified metadata
  AssertionError: expected [ 'intent' ] to deeply equal [ 'intent', 'put', 'commit' ]

FAIL src/pages/assets.test.tsx > presigned large-object upload > surfaces a gateway commit error verbatim in an alert
  Expected: "sha256 mismatch: declared aaa… but staged bytes hash to bbb…"
  Received: "Upload failed RequestInit: Expected signal (\"AbortSignal {}\") to be an instance of AbortSignal."

FAIL src/pages/assets.test.tsx > presigned upload cancellation > cancels an in-flight upload and reports it as cancelled, never as published
  AssertionError: expected false to be true
```

## Root cause

`src/lib/gateway-client.ts` normalizes a cross-realm `AbortSignal` in exactly one
of its four `fetch` call sites. `gatewayRequest` (line ~210) guards:

```ts
if (signal) {
  try {
    // Embedded/test DOMs can expose Request and AbortSignal from different
    // realms. Browsers accept this path; incompatible realms must not turn
    // an otherwise valid Admin API request into a synchronous TypeError.
    new Request("data:,", { signal });
  } catch {
    signal = undefined;
  }
}
```

The presigned direct-bucket PUT at **`src/lib/gateway-client.ts:420`** passes the
same `signal` straight through with no such guard:

```ts
const response = await fetch(uploadUrl, { method: "PUT", headers, body, signal });
```

Under jsdom the signal comes from a different realm than the `fetch`
implementation, so this throws synchronously — the PUT never fires, the flow
stops after `intent`, and the cancellation path reports the realm TypeError
instead of the real outcome.

The comment at `gateway-client.ts:213` states the intended contract ("incompatible
realms must not turn an otherwise valid request into a synchronous TypeError").
The PUT leg — per its own `#344` comment the leg an operator most needs to
cancel — does not honour it.

## Fix

Extract the realm-compat normalization into one helper and apply it at every
`fetch` site that accepts a caller-supplied `signal` (lines 221, 325, 420, 439),
rather than repeating the guard by hand at one of them.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `npx vitest run` is green in `admin-console` on `main`.
- [ ] The normalization is applied at **every** `signal`-accepting `fetch` site, from a single shared helper.
- [ ] A test pins the contract for the PUT leg specifically: a cross-realm signal must not abort the flow, and a same-realm signal must still cancel the in-flight PUT. Verified by mutation — removing the guard must turn the test red.

Found by the test gate while gating #348. See also #531 (admin-console has no CI at all, which is why this went unobserved).

labels.name: priority:p1
labels.description: High-value enterprise capability after P0 foundations

title: [admin-console][assets][P1] Presigned PUT drops the cross-realm AbortSignal guard — 3 vitest failures, main is red

body:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/` contains **14 workflows, none of which mention `admin-console`**:

```
$ grep -rl "admin-console" .github/
(no output)
```

So `tsc -b`, `eslint`, `vitest`, `vite build`, `check:bundle`, `check:api-types`
and the Playwright specs are **never run by CI**. Every frontend claim on this
repo rests entirely on a dev agent running the commands locally and pasting the
numbers into an issue comment — nothing re-checks them after the branch lands.

This is not hypothetical. As of `e3ed951` (2026-07-27) `main` is red on **two**
independent admin-console gates that no one noticed:

- `npx tsc -b` → 1 error (tracked separately in #527, red since #474 on 2026-07-25)
- `npx vitest run` → **3 failed / 614 passed** in `src/pages/assets.test.tsx` (filed alongside this issue)

Both went unobserved for days across multiple frontend issues that each reported
"tsc 0 errors, vitest N pass" in their landing comments.

## Why it matters

#348's entire acceptance is a *completeness* claim ("every registered route is
usable in en + zh-CN"). A completeness claim that is only ever checked on the
author's machine decays silently the moment anyone adds a route or a literal.
The `ferrogate/no-untranslated-literal` rule and the catalog-parity test are both
genuinely good (both survive mutation — verified by the test gate 2026-07-27),
and both are worth exactly nothing if no automated run ever invokes them.

## Scope

- Add an `admin-console` CI workflow triggered on changes under `admin-console/**`:
  `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npx tsc -b`, `npx tsc -p tsconfig.e2e.json --noEmit`,
  `npx vitest run`, `npm run build` (which chains `check:bundle`), `npm run check:api-types`.
- Add the Playwright leg (`npm run test:e2e:install` + `npm run test:e2e`) — the
  dual-locale route sweep is 121 cases and has, to date, **never been executed
  anywhere that leaves a record**.
- Make it a required check so a red `main` cannot recur unobserved.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A workflow runs the full admin-console gate on every PR touching `admin-console/**` and on pushes to `main`.
- [ ] The Playwright dual-locale sweep runs in CI with browsers installed.
- [ ] Deliberately breaking each leg (a type error, a lint literal, a dropped zh-CN key, a bundle-budget bump) turns the workflow red — verified by mutation, not by inspection.

labels.name: priority:p1
labels.description: High-value enterprise capability after P0 foundations

body:
Found by the #345 code review while checking whether the console discriminates the bind response.

## Problem

`handle_admin_site_domain_bind` returns `match (proven, existing.is_some())`:

- **202** when the binding is recorded but **unproven** — and the gateway deliberately keeps that hostname *out* of the ACME set (`site_domains.rs:513-517`, `:533-537`)
- **200** when re-binding an already-proven hostname
- **201** when creating a proven one

`docs/openapi/admin-api.openapi.json` declares only **200 and 201** for `bindSiteDomain`. The 202 is undeclared.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

The 202 is the *semantically interesting* case: it is the one where the operator has bound a hostname that will **not serve**. A generated client that switches on the declared response set has no branch for it, which is precisely the shape of bug #345 was bounced for twice — a 2xx that does not mean what the success path assumes.

The console side is now handled (`f504810` derives its claim from `site_domain.serving` rather than the status), so this is a contract-hygiene issue rather than a live defect.

## Scope

- Declare the 202 on `bindSiteDomain` with its schema, and describe what distinguishes it from 200/201.
- This touches the reviewed compatibility baseline, so it needs the baseline revision that `scripts/check-openapi.py` enforces — that is why #345 deliberately did not fix it in place.
- Check whether the same undeclared-status pattern exists on sibling site-domain operations while you are in there.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `bindSiteDomain` declares 200, 201 and 202, each with its schema and a description that says what it means operationally.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check-openapi.py` passes, baseline revised deliberately rather than regenerated blindly.
- [ ] A test pins the gateway's three-way return against the declared set, so they cannot drift again.
title: [api-contract][P3] bindSiteDomain returns an undeclared 202 — the spec claims only 200/201

body:
Follow-up flagged by the #259 code review and worth filing **now rather than earlier**, because it only became the real number once every read path was bounded.

## Why now

Before `5107f74`, three of the four bucket-backed read paths were unbounded, so "peak memory" was dominated by a single unbounded request and `max_gateway_buffer_bytes` did not describe the system. After it, every buffering read goes through one chokepoint with a byte budget, so peak memory is genuinely:

```
max_gateway_buffer_bytes  ×  concurrent bucket-backed reads
```

**Nothing bounds the second factor.** At the 10 MiB default, N concurrent `fetch_asset` / MCP `resources/read` / site-serve / presigned-commit requests hold N × 10 MiB, uncapped. The runbook's "Sizing a box" section (added in `5107f74`) states this plainly — it is documented, not hidden — but documenting a limit is not enforcing one.

## Scope

- Add admission control for the buffering read path: a semaphore or in-flight-byte budget, sized from config, that queues or sheds rather than allocating.
- Shedding must be **honest and typed** — a `503` naming the condition, not a truncated body and not a silent wait that looks like slowness.
- Decide and document the interaction with the presigned commit path, which is already streaming and O(chunk); it should not consume the buffering budget it does not need.
- Update the runbook's sizing formula once the second factor is bounded, so the number an operator sizes from is the enforced one.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A configured ceiling on concurrent buffering reads (or on total in-flight buffered bytes) is enforced, not just documented.
- [ ] Exceeding it produces a typed, named refusal — no truncation, no unbounded queueing.
- [ ] A test drives more concurrent over-budget reads than the ceiling and asserts the enforced behaviour, with a measured memory ceiling in the same shape as `a_100mb_object_completes_the_presigned_lifecycle_with_flat_gateway_rss`.
- [ ] The streaming commit path is confirmed not to consume the buffering budget.
- [ ] `docs/assets/private-bucket-migration.md`'s "Sizing a box" section describes the enforced bound.

## Context

Per-operation bound and its chokepoint guard: `5107f74` (#259). The guard test `the_buffering_bucket_read_is_only_called_from_the_bounded_chokepoint` names any new caller by file and line, so a fifth read surface cannot silently escape the per-operation bound — but it inherits the unbounded aggregate too.

labels.name: priority:p2
labels.description: Validated follow-up; do not pull ahead of P0/P1

title: [gateway-core][P2] No admission control on bucket-backed reads — per-operation memory is bounded, aggregate is not

body:
Found by the test gate while gating #344. **Not a #344 defect** — it is an API gap the console cannot work around, so it is filed on its own.

`crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/assets.rs:880` and `asset_presign.rs:1116` return `200 AssetMutationResponse` even when screening records `pending_scan` or `quarantined` (`asset_security.rs:432,455-461`).

The console then shows *"Asset pushed"* / *"Large object committed"* while the row is filtered out of `GET /v1/assets` by `is_downloadable()` (`assets.rs:340`). So the operator is told the push succeeded and then cannot find the asset.

**`AssetSummary` carries no visibility field**, so the console has nothing to discriminate on. This is why it is an API gap rather than a console bug — no frontend change can fix it.

## Reachability

Unreachable on default config: `async_threshold_bytes` defaults to `None` and the default scan backend is Eicar → `Clean`. Reachable with a configured async threshold or an out-of-process scanner — i.e. exactly the production posture.

## Relationship to #379

#379's withheld-assets page is the compensating surface. This issue is about the **push response** being indistinguishable from a committed one, which #379 does not address: even with that page shipped, the push toast still lies at the moment it matters.

## Ask

- Decide the contract for a withheld push: a distinct 2xx (e.g. `202` with a `withheld` state), or `200` carrying an explicit visibility/screening field on `AssetMutationResponse`.
- Whichever is chosen, surface it on `AssetSummary` too, so a listing can show *withheld* rather than silently omitting the row.
- Cover it in the harness. `asset-registry-api` (landed in `c42dcb0`) is the natural home. The test must go **red** if the withheld case becomes indistinguishable from a committed one again.

Refs #344, #379.

labels.name: priority:p2
labels.description: Validated follow-up; do not pull ahead of P0/P1

body:
Found by the test gate while gating #344.

```
$ npx tsc -b
src/pages/agent-jobs.tsx(85,43): error TS2345:
  Argument of type '...' is not assignable to parameter of type '...'.
  Property 'required_capabilities' is missing
```

`submitAgentJob` is called without the now-required `required_capabilities`. Introduced by `928e82c` "(#474) Address code-review blockers on the async agent-job surface" (2026-07-25).

## Why it matters more than one type error

`npx tsc -b` is part of the admin-console gate. While it is red, **every frontend issue inherits a failure that is not its own** — which is precisely the dynamic that trains people to skip a gate. We have now watched that happen twice in this repo:

- #509: `cargo clippy` sat red on `main` for a day; three separate slices ran package-scoped clippy, got a clean result for their own crate, and shipped.
- #510: seven vitest failures were reported as "known pre-existing, unrelated" by several gate runs — they turned out to be a 13-line jsdom polyfill gap **masking the acceptance-critical publish-path coverage** of an entire issue.

A stable, well-understood red is more dangerous than a flaky one, because it stops being read.

## A measurement gotcha worth recording

`npx tsc -b | tail` reports `$?` of `tail`, not of `tsc`. The real exit code only shows on an unpiped run. Any report claiming "tsc clean" from a piped invocation should be re-checked.

## Ask

- Pass `required_capabilities` at `agent-jobs.tsx:85` (or make it optional if that is the intended contract — decide which, do not just silence the type).
- A test that fails if the typecheck regresses, so this cannot sit red again.

## Verification

```
cd admin-console && npx tsc -b        # unpiped; must exit 0
```

Refs #474, #344, #509, #510.

labels.name: priority:p1
labels.description: High-value enterprise capability after P0 foundations

body:
Split out of #353 because it is **not an x402 defect** — it is live on the ordinary governed REST path and predates x402 entirely.

## The leak

`crates/agent-worker/src/external_actions.rs`, `run_authorized_rest_action` → `GovernedRestExecution::response_excerpt`, recorded as `response_excerpt` in `rest.requested` event metadata and interpolated into `GovernedWorkloadOutcome.output` for the self-hosted governed-family path (`:4030`).

The excerpt was `response.chars().take(512).collect()` over the **raw HTTP response including the status line and every header**. Any `authorization`, `cookie` or `set-cookie` an upstream returns is recorded **verbatim, in full**, into worker events and worker stdout.

## Reachable and demonstrated

A loopback origin returning `authorization: Bearer super-secret-token` and `set-cookie: session=abc123` puts both into `events[1].metadata["response_excerpt"]`. Under the mutation test written for #353, the panic output prints the recorded value in the clear.

## Since when

Present since the #247 governed REST executor landed — the excerpt line is unchanged from its introduction.

x402 **raises the severity rather than changing its kind**: `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` carries a signed, submittable SVM transaction, so recording it is recording spendable value, not just a credential.

## Status

**Fixed for the REST path** in `8d5d700` (#353): bearer header *values* are replaced before truncation, header *names* survive, and `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`/`PAYMENT-RESPONSE` are deliberately kept because they are public protocol evidence #354 needs. Proven by `recorded_rest_evidence_never_carries_bearer_material` and `redaction_precedes_truncation_so_no_proof_prefix_survives`; removing the redaction call fails both.

## What this issue is for — the unswept surfaces

**Other families were not audited.** They record excerpts through their own metadata builders — `output_excerpt`, `value_excerpt`, `page_state` — and none of them was reviewed for the same pattern.

## Scope

- Audit every metadata/excerpt builder in `agent-worker` for raw-response or raw-header capture, not just the REST family.
- Route them through one shared redaction helper rather than repeating the fix per family — a per-family copy is what let this survive in three other builders.
- Add a regression test at the shared chokepoint so a **new** family inherits the redaction, and one that fails if a future edit records a header value verbatim.
- Decide whether recorded evidence should carry header values at all, or only a whitelist. The #353 fix keeps names and drops bearer values; the other families may not need values either.

## Acceptance

- [ ] No `agent-worker` metadata builder records an upstream `authorization`, `cookie`, `set-cookie` or `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` value.
- [ ] A single shared helper does the redaction; a grep proves there is no second copy.
- [ ] A test fails if a new excerpt path bypasses it.
- [ ] The audit result is recorded here — including any family found clean, so the next reader does not redo it.

labels.name: priority:p1
labels.description: High-value enterprise capability after P0 foundations
