body:
Parent: #270.
Related: #260, #338.

## Problem

Inline asset PUT enforces immutability with a read-before-write check followed later by an ordinary repository upsert. Two concurrent first pushes can both observe no row and then overwrite each other.

With memory or inline Postgres bytes, the last upsert wins. With bucket-backed inline storage, both requests also write the same object key before the metadata upsert, so the winning metadata hash can reference bytes written by the losing request.

#338 adds a create-if-absent primitive and hardens the presigned staging/final path. The ordinary inline path still needs the same publication invariant; switching only the row write to CAS is insufficient while concurrent bucket writes share a key.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every inline publish attempt writes bucket bytes to a unique or content-addressed final candidate that another attempt cannot overwrite.
- [ ] Metadata publication uses repository create-if-absent, never an immutable-version upsert.
- [ ] Exactly one concurrent first push becomes visible; losers return typed 409 and clean only their own unreferenced candidates.
- [ ] A mutation error distinguishes definitive pre-commit failure from outcome unknown and never deletes a possibly referenced winner.
- [ ] Memory and Postgres implementations share the same truth table.
- [ ] Barrier/channel concurrency tests prove different-content first pushes cannot produce row/object hash mismatch.
- [ ] Local bucket E2E verifies the stored bytes, metadata hash, list/manifest, and download all belong to the same winner.
- [ ] Live Supabase proof is bounded, uses a unique per-run schema, and performs no load testing.

## Non-goals

- Changing yank/unyank updates, which legitimately mutate an existing row.
- Long transactions or bucket work inside a database transaction.

labels.name: priority:p1
labels.description: High-value enterprise capability after P0 foundations

title: [assets][P1] Make inline immutable publication atomic across concurrent first pushes

body:
Parent: #270.
Related: #259, #338.

## Problem

The presigned PUT signer currently signs only the host header and uses UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD. The upload-intent endpoint preflights the declared size and SHA-256, but the bucket does not enforce either value when accepting the direct PUT.

#338 isolates every intent in staging and prevents a replay from mutating committed bytes. That closes immutable-object corruption, but a writer can still upload a staging object larger than the per-object or tenant quota and leave it until best-effort cleanup or GC. Commit rejects the object later; bucket capacity was already consumed.

## Required invariant

The direct bucket write must be cryptographically bound to the constraints the gateway approved, or use an equivalent bucket-native mechanism that rejects mismatched bytes before storing them.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Upload intent returns the exact required request headers or fields for the direct PUT.
- [ ] SigV4 or the selected bucket-native primitive binds content length and a strong payload checksum; changing either invalidates the upload authorization.
- [ ] The implementation is verified against Supabase Storage S3 compatibility with bounded small functional objects before claiming support.
- [ ] Local SigV4 tests prove wrong size, wrong checksum, omitted required headers, and replay with different bytes are rejected at the bucket boundary.
- [ ] Multipart behavior, maximum object size, URL expiry, and abort or orphan cleanup are explicit and typed.
- [ ] Operator metrics and audit evidence distinguish intent rejection, bucket rejection, commit rejection, and orphan GC.
- [ ] No load, stress, or sustained-throughput test runs against Supabase.

## Non-goals

- Replacing S3-compatible storage.
- Relying on commit-time validation as the only quota control.

body:
Parent: #270.
Related: #260, #338.

## Problem

Channel move currently performs two independent repository operations:

1. list/read variants and confirm the requested version is currently non-yanked;
2. upsert the channel row.

A concurrent delete or yank can land between those operations, so the durable channel can point at an absent or non-resolvable version. The inverse race also exists after a successful move because yank/delete does not update or reject affected channels as one invariant.

#338 fixes fabricated 200 responses for already-missing targets and storage errors, and documents the current preflight honestly. It does not make the lifecycle invariant atomic.

## Runtime impact

An operator can receive a successful channel move and later find that the same channel cannot resolve. Under incident pressure there is no durable evidence that distinguishes a valid target at commit time from a stale pointer created by a race.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Define the channel/version truth table for move, yank, unyank, variant delete, and whole-version delete.
- [ ] Postgres enforces each coordination mutation with one short conditional DML/CTE, or the smallest irreducible transaction with bounded lock/statement timeout.
- [ ] The memory backend performs the equivalent check/mutation under one lock.
- [ ] A move returns success only when its target is durably resolvable under the chosen invariant.
- [ ] Yank/delete either reject while referenced or atomically move/remove affected channels according to the documented policy.
- [ ] Audit evidence records the prior target, requested target, outcome, and request ID.
- [ ] Barrier/channel-based concurrency tests cover move-vs-yank and move-vs-delete; no timing sleeps.
- [ ] Contract/compliance and local E2E prove no successful operation leaves a dangling channel.
- [ ] Live Supabase coverage uses a unique per-run schema and bounded functional traffic only.

## Non-goals

- Dependency graphs or cross-registry mirroring.
- Long transactions, database retry loops, or performance tests against Supabase.

labels.name: priority:p1
labels.description: High-value enterprise capability after P0 foundations

title: [assets][P1] Preserve channel target integrity across concurrent lifecycle changes

body:
Parent: #270.
Related: #179, #259, #261, #338.

## Problem

The inline asset publish path calls `asset_security::screen_asset_push`, which applies detached-signature verification, cross-tenant approval, the configured malware scanner, and emits verification evidence.

The presigned commit path currently calls only `validate_asset_content` after size/SHA-256 verification. It therefore bypasses the signature requirement, approval gate, pluggable scanner, and evidence path that #261 declared complete. The old comments and runbook overstated parity; #338 narrows those claims, but documentation is not a security control.

There is a related visibility gap: `screen_asset_push` can return `pending_scan` or `quarantined`, yet the persisted asset model does not carry that state and the registry/download path does not demonstrably withhold it.

## First-principles constraint

A publish surface must not choose a weaker trust policy because the bytes arrived through a different transport. Inline and presigned uploads need one shared screening/publication contract, with inspectable evidence and an explicit visibility state.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Inline and presigned commits invoke the same signature, approval, scanner, and content-policy service over the final verified bytes.
- [ ] Presigned requests carry the signature/visibility/approval inputs required by that service, with typed contract schemas and errors.
- [ ] Scan/signature/approval evidence is durable and linked to the asset, tenant, request ID, and audit event.
- [ ] Pending/quarantined assets are persisted with explicit state but are absent from list/manifest/channel/range resolution and cannot receive ordinary or presigned downloads until promoted clean.
- [ ] Scanner unavailable/reject, invalid signature, and missing approval fail closed with focused async tests.
- [ ] Contract/compliance and local E2E prove identical decisions for inline and presigned publication.
- [ ] Live Supabase proof uses a unique per-run schema and bounded functional traffic only.

## Non-goals

- Replacing the scanner backends.
- Load or performance testing against Supabase.

labels.name: priority:p1
labels.description: High-value enterprise capability after P0 foundations

title: [assets][P1][security] Enforce full trust screening on presigned commits

Manual command lists will drift as the Control Plane API evolves. The epic is not complete if a route exists in OpenAPI but is silently unreachable from the CLI, or if a command returns success while the runtime ignores the mutation.

## Scope

- Maintain a machine-readable mapping from every public OpenAPI operation ID to its CLI resource/verb, with reviewed exclusions carrying owner and technical reason.

- Generate complete command reference, examples, migration notes from legacy admin-api naming/flags, and shell completions for supported shells.
- Include the CLI in local build/release packaging and supply-chain/signing evidence. Keep GitHub Actions release:published-only; do not add per-commit cloud workflows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The coverage report accounts for every public OpenAPI operation ID and fails on an unreviewed gap or duplicate command mapping.
- [ ] Contract tests prove request shape, response/error decoding, status/exit mapping, pagination, secret redaction, and request/trace/audit attribution.

- [ ] The parent epic remains open until the parity report is complete; partial scaffolding or selected command families do not satisfy completion.

- Build and test the Rust CLI as a supported release artifact, not an internal developer helper.

body:
Parent: #358. Depends on #360.

## Scope

Expose the non-trivial action surfaces that generic CRUD cannot represent:

- Agent runs and timelines; schedules, fire history, run-now, enable/disable, and cancellation where the API supports it.
- Self-hosted worker registration, certificate issuance/rotation/revocation, events/checkpoints/runs, managed worker pools, and managed sessions.
- MCP server/identity operations, tool catalog and tool sessions.
- Tool approval list/get/approve/deny/expire with immutable fingerprint and actor evidence.
- Guardrail policies and revisions, activate/rollback/dry-run, evaluations, and investigation views.

## Safety and evidence requirements

- Destructive or irreversible actions require an interactive confirmation when a TTY is present and explicit --yes in non-interactive mode.
- Approval, certificate, policy-promotion, rollback, and run actions must print the resulting state plus request/trace/run/audit correlation IDs.
- The CLI must not poll forever. Wait/watch behavior needs explicit timeout, terminal-state handling, and cancellation semantics.
- Do not reproduce scheduling, approval, guardrail, or worker lifecycle rules client-side; submit typed intent and report server decisions.

## Acceptance criteria

## Problem

The existing assets, plans, and reload clients each own connection flags and response handling. Copying that pattern across more than 200 API operations would produce inconsistent authentication, output, pagination, and errors.

## Scope

- Add named contexts for endpoint, default tenant/project/workspace, TLS/CA settings, and credential source. Do not persist bearer tokens in plaintext by default; support environment/stdin or another explicit secret source.
- Define global overrides for context, endpoint, token source, timeout, output, and non-interactive operation with deterministic precedence over environment and context values.
- Build one typed Control Plane API transport used by all remote commands. Preserve HTTP status, API error code/message/details, request ID, trace ID, retry hints, and pagination metadata.
- Provide human-readable table output and stable machine-readable JSON. stdout is data; diagnostics and progress go to stderr.
- Define stable exit-code classes for usage/configuration, authentication/authorization, not found/conflict, validation, transport/timeout, and server failure.
- Support list pagination, filtering, sorting, and explicit all-pages behavior without silently truncating results.
- Move one narrow vertical slice, including ops status, onto the shared client and lock the patterns with dedicated tests before broad resource work.
- Preserve compatibility for existing assets/plans/reload flags while preparing them to use the shared context and transport.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Context create/list/show/use/delete works without printing secrets.
- [ ] Environment/global flag/context precedence is documented and covered by unit tests.
- [ ] Table and JSON output, error envelopes, exit codes, pagination, timeout, TLS failure, request ID, and wrong-scope behavior are tested.
- [ ] A real ferrogate-test scenario runs a CLI status read and one authorized mutation through the standalone Control Plane API, then proves the durable/API-visible result and audit evidence.
- [ ] Test bodies live in dedicated sibling or integration test files; production CLI modules contain only minimal test wiring.

## Rust module architecture and product constraints

- Implement this foundation in Rust. Reuse Clap for parsing and the workspace async HTTP/TLS stack; do not shell out to curl or embed a second TypeScript/Python client.
- Split command parsing/dispatch, context storage, typed Control Plane API transport, output rendering, and error/exit mapping into explicit modules with narrow interfaces.
- Resource command families register compile-time command metadata used by help and the OpenAPI coverage manifest. Adding a resource must not require editing unrelated transport or renderer code.

- Add CLI/API version reporting and a tested compatibility check so an unsupported server contract fails with an actionable message rather than mis-decoding responses.

body:
Parent: #271. Related control-plane client: #295 and #313.

Origin: user directive 2026-07-22 — every FerroGate resource that can be managed from the Admin Console must also be manageable from a Docker-style command-line interface.

## Problem

The existing ferrogate binary is a service launcher plus a small set of disconnected operator utilities. It currently has isolated commands such as assets, plans, reload, validate, and storage migration, but it is not a coherent remote control-plane client. Operators cannot script the same resource lifecycle that the Admin Console exposes, and command behavior, credentials, output, errors, and coverage are not governed by one contract.

## Product and architecture decision

- Extend the existing ferrogate binary as the canonical management CLI in the first delivery. Do not create a second ferrogatectl binary that duplicates packaging, authentication, and command discovery without a proven need.
- Treat the Admin Console and CLI as peer clients of one authenticated public FerroGate Control Plane API.
- The REST API is the source of truth. Remote CLI commands must never bypass policy/audit by reading or writing the database directly.
- Promote the service name from Admin API to FerroGate Control Plane API. OpenAPI is the machine-readable contract for that service; OpenAPI is not the service's product name.
- Public means a supported external REST contract. It does not mean anonymous or unrestricted access: authentication, tenant isolation, RBAC scopes, audit evidence, and safe mutation semantics remain mandatory.
- Preserve existing command and /admin/v1 compatibility during a documented migration window. Avoid a flag-day rename.

## Command model

Use predictable noun/verb commands with shared flags and script-safe output, for example:

    ferrogate context use production
    ferrogate tenants list --output json
    ferrogate providers get provider-id
    ferrogate guardrail-policies activate policy-id --revision revision-id
    ferrogate ops status

Existing plural commands such as assets and plans remain compatible while they move onto the shared transport and output contract.

## Delivery slices

1. Canonical Control Plane API naming and compatibility migration.
2. CLI contexts, authentication, HTTP transport, pagination, output, and error foundation.
3. Organization, IAM, policy, provider, model, and gateway-configuration resource coverage.
4. Agent, worker, MCP, tool, approval, and guardrail lifecycle coverage.
5. Asset registry and static-site/domain lifecycle coverage.
6. Billing, usage, evidence, and operator-action coverage.
7. OpenAPI operation coverage gate, contract/E2E proof, documentation, completion, and release packaging.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every public Control Plane API operation has a discoverable CLI command or an explicit reviewed exclusion with a technical reason.
- [ ] A machine-readable coverage check compares CLI coverage to OpenAPI operation IDs and fails when the API adds an uncovered operation.
- [ ] All commands share contexts, credential handling, timeouts/TLS, pagination/filtering, request/trace attribution, structured errors, and stable JSON output.
- [ ] Mutations preserve API authorization, tenant scope, idempotency/concurrency contracts, audit evidence, and confirmation behavior for destructive actions.
- [ ] Focused unit/contract tests and ferrogate-test E2E scenarios prove representative read, create/update, action, failure, and delete paths through the real Control Plane API.
- [ ] The Admin Console and CLI use the same public API contract; neither maintains a private parallel resource model.
- [ ] Reference documentation and shell completions make the supported resource/verb surface discoverable.

## Non-goals

- Reimplementing server business rules in the CLI.
- Direct database administration disguised as resource management.
- Making inference/data-plane endpoints or privileged control-plane routes anonymous.
- Closing this epic after only scaffolding or a few CRUD commands.

## Product-grade Rust CLI constraints

- Implement the CLI in Rust as a first-class FerroGate workspace product, building on the existing ferrogate-cli binary and Clap command model.
- Keep ferrogate-cli as the composition/UX boundary. Put the reusable typed Control Plane API client and shared schemas behind the existing ferrogate-admin boundary or a narrowly justified dedicated crate; do not duplicate server contracts inside every command.
- Organize each resource family as a narrow command module with shared descriptors/interfaces for dispatch, help, and OpenAPI coverage. Do not grow one giant command match or hand-copy transport/error logic for hundreds of endpoints.
- Extensible means a new API resource can add a module and coverage mapping without changing unrelated command families. It does not require runtime-loaded CLI plugins or an opaque dynamic command system.
- Treat flags, resource/verb names, JSON schemas, exit codes, and stdout/stderr separation as a versioned product contract. Breaking CLI changes require an explicit compatibility/deprecation path.
- Ship release-grade Rust binaries for supported platforms with version metadata, shell completions, checksums, signatures/SBOM evidence, and reproducible release instructions.
- New dependencies require a concrete reduction in complexity or risk; prefer existing workspace HTTP, serialization, TLS, and error infrastructure.

body:
Parent: #267 · Refs #287 (real worker identities), #294 (activity evidence), #313 (Admin Console coverage)

## Summary

FerroGate currently presents two agent execution identities:

1. managed workers/sessions, whose lifecycle FerroGate controls;
2. self-hosted workers, whose registered identity and heartbeats FerroGate verifies.

A third operator-visible situation exists: a caller directly uses a durable platform virtual API key against inference/resource routes without any verified managed session, self-hosted worker, or agent run identity. The traffic belongs to the key's tenant/project/workspace and consumes gateway resources, but FerroGate cannot truthfully identify the calling agent.

Surface this as tenant-scoped **Unknown agent activity** with `status = running` while recent requests are observed.

## Critical semantic decision

This is a third **presentation/source category**, not a third `WorkerType` and not a synthetic persistent Agent entity.

One virtual API key may be shared by multiple agents, SDKs, scripts, or users. FerroGate cannot infer process identity or cardinality from the credential. The API/UI must therefore say "unattributed activity observed through this key," not claim that exactly one real agent exists.

Proposed view contract:

```json
{
  "id": "observed:<tenant_id>:<api_key_id>",
  "source": "virtual_api_key",
  "identity_status": "unattributed",
  "display_name": "Unknown",
  "status": "running",
  "status_basis": "recent_api_key_activity",
  "tenant_id": "...",
  "project_id": "...",
  "workspace_id": "...",
  "api_key_id": "...",
  "credential_name": "optional redacted operator hint",
  "first_seen_at_unix": 0,
  "last_seen_at_unix": 0,
  "running_ttl_seconds": 60
}
```

The exact endpoint/schema name can change, but these semantics cannot.

## Attribution precedence

For every authenticated request, choose the first verified identity:

1. verified managed-worker session;
2. verified self-hosted worker/run;
3. verified agent-run/workflow correlation;
4. otherwise, if authentication used a durable virtual API key, record `virtual_api_key + unattributed` presence.

A caller-supplied `agent_run_id`, header, user-agent, model name, or display name is not verified identity and must not suppress Unknown activity. YAML fallback keys without a durable tenant/project/workspace owner are out of scope for the first slice.

## Runtime and storage shape

- `ferrogate-cli` authentication already resolves durable keys to `TenantContext` containing tenant/project/workspace/api-key IDs. Touch observed activity only after successful authentication and tenant/quota gates.
- Add a narrow `ObservedAgentPresenceRepository` contract in `ferrogate-storage`, keyed by `(tenant_id, api_key_id)`, with `first_seen`, monotonic `last_seen`, scope IDs, and evidence counters/links.
- Do not synchronously write Postgres on every request. Enqueue/coalesce presence touches through the existing deferred evidence writer or another bounded async projection, at most once per configured interval per key.
- The durable mutation is one short indexed UPSERT/CAS. No transaction, wait, external call, or full request-log scan.
- `running` is a derived presence state: `now - last_seen <= configured TTL`. It means recently observed traffic, not a confirmed live process. Expiry produces `inactive`/absence automatically; it does not fabricate a stop event.
- Key rotation preserves the same durable key ID and presence row. Disable/revoke prevents new touches; historical last-seen evidence remains tenant-visible, but `running` expires by TTL.

## API and Admin Console

Add a tenant-scoped agent-presence/inventory read model that can display managed, self-hosted, and unattributed virtual-key activity together while preserving their different trust levels.

For unattributed rows:

- `display_name` is exactly `Unknown` at the API contract level; the UI may localize the label.
- Show the virtual-key name/last4 only as a separate credential hint the tenant is already authorized to view. Never use it as the inferred agent name.
- Show `last_seen`, status basis, project/workspace, request/token/cost activity for the same key and time window when available.
- Do not expose plaintext key, key hash, proof, raw prompts/responses, or another tenant's identifiers.
- Do not add the row to agent-run timelines unless a real run identity exists.

## E2E closure

- **Operator input:** create tenant A/project/workspace and a durable virtual API key, then call a normal gateway inference/resource route directly with that key and no verified agent identity.
- **Execution:** successful auth emits a coalesced presence touch attributed from the key's stored ownership; the tenant-scoped presence API derives `running` from recent activity.
- **Observable evidence:** tenant A sees one row with `source=virtual_api_key`, `identity_status=unattributed`, `display_name=Unknown`, the correct scope/key ID, last-seen timestamp, and matching usage counters.
- **Failure behavior:** tenant B cannot see it; invalid/revoked keys do not create/touch it; a verified managed/self-hosted request is not duplicated as Unknown; TTL expiry stops reporting `running`.
- **Regression:** deterministic clock/barrier tests cover concurrency and TTL. No timing sleeps.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A direct request authenticated by a durable virtual API key produces one tenant/key-scoped Unknown presence row without requiring agent headers or registration.
- [ ] N concurrent requests through the same key still produce one presence identity; timestamps/counters are monotonic and no hot-path synchronous database write is added.
- [ ] The implementation never claims how many real agents share the key. Stable identity is explicitly the observed key activity, not a process/agent UUID.
- [ ] Verified managed and self-hosted traffic keeps its real identity and does not also appear as Unknown.
- [ ] Spoofed agent/run headers cannot upgrade attribution or hide unattributed activity.
- [ ] Tenant/project/workspace/key ownership is taken from durable authentication, not request payload, and tenant isolation is enforced before pagination/aggregation.
- [ ] `running` uses an operator-visible typed TTL and exposes `status_basis=recent_api_key_activity`; deterministic tests prove the exact boundary.
- [ ] Disabled/revoked/expired keys cannot refresh presence. Rotation does not create a duplicate row.
- [ ] Request count, token usage, and cost shown for the row match existing key-scoped usage/billing evidence for the same window; missing evidence is shown as unavailable, never invented.
- [ ] Admin API/OpenAPI and console display include source/trust/status basis, display `Unknown`, and avoid leaking key material or request bodies.
- [ ] A focused E2E proves operator input, runtime touch, durable projection, tenant-scoped API output, UI mapping, TTL expiry, and cross-tenant denial.

## Non-goals

- Fingerprinting callers from User-Agent, IP, model, prompt, or TLS properties.
- Treating every API client as a registered Agent or creating `StoredAgentRun` rows without a run.
- Estimating agent cardinality behind a shared key.
- Changing managed/self-hosted worker lifecycle semantics.

## Verification

Focused `ferrogate-storage`, `ferrogate-cli`, observability/usage, and Admin Console tests; OpenAPI check; deterministic cross-tenant E2E; clippy/static gates. Runtime performance proof must confirm the presence projection adds no synchronous Postgres work to the request hot path.

Parent: #349 · Depends on #350 · Priority P2, independent of the outbound P1 chain

## Problem

There is a second, distinct product path: external agents pay to call FerroGate-hosted APIs. pay.sh already provides a declarative `pay server` proxy for this. Embedding its axum middleware into Pingora or reusing the outbound wallet state machine would add coupling without proving demand.

## Decision for this slice

Validate inbound monetization as a **sidecar/reverse-proxy deployment**, not in-process middleware:

`external x402 client -> pay.sh pay server -> private FerroGate upstream`

Start with one fixed-price, non-streaming endpoint. Variable token-priced inference, streaming usage settlement, subscriptions, MPP, and catalog publishing stay out until the fixed-price trust and attribution loop is proven.

## Scope and ownership

- Add a reviewed provider YAML and deployment manifest/example for pay.sh with explicit Solana network, USDC mint/recipient, fixed price, health probe, and secret references.
- Prevent bypass of the pay.sh edge by keeping the FerroGate upstream private or requiring a short-lived signed/mTLS sidecar assertion.
- Map verified payer, transaction, price, and pay.sh request identity into FerroGate request/tenant attribution without trusting caller-supplied headers.
- Define whether inbound x402 creates a new tenant, maps to a product/public tenant, or requires existing auth. Do not silently mix payer wallet identity with FerroGate tenant identity.
- Keep stablecoin revenue evidence separate from Stripe top-ups and outbound agent-spend records while exposing one coherent Admin view.

## E2E closure

- **Operator input:** deploy one local/sandbox pay.sh sidecar spec in front of one fixed-price FerroGate test route.
- **Execution:** unpaid request receives 402; pay.sh-compatible client pays; sidecar verifies/settles and forwards exactly once.
- **Failure behavior:** direct upstream bypass, invalid proof, wrong network/mint, replay, and settlement failure never reach the protected handler.
- **Evidence:** FerroGate request log and Admin API show payer/transaction/price/sidecar identity correlated to request/trace ID, with no proof or key leakage.
- **Regression:** local sandbox E2E needs no mainnet funds.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Architecture threat model covers bypass, spoofed forwarding headers, replay, duplicate forwarding, sidecar compromise, secret rotation, timeout after settlement, and upstream 5xx.
- [ ] Only one fixed-price non-streaming route is enabled; no claim of token-accurate inference billing is made.
- [ ] The sidecar cannot reach Admin APIs and the public cannot reach the protected upstream directly.
- [ ] A settled request is forwarded once and attributed durably; duplicate payment/retry is idempotent.
- [ ] Revenue/payment evidence is queryable without mutating the prepaid-credit wallet unless an explicit, separately tested conversion/top-up operation exists.
- [ ] Local deployment and `pay --sandbox curl` compatibility are documented and tested; mainnet and catalog publication require a separate operator decision.

## Verification

Local container/process topology with pay.sh sandbox/local mode, focused route E2E, deployment manifest validation, OpenAPI/schema checks for added evidence surfaces, and no production/mainnet transaction.

Parent: #349 · Depends on #352 and #353

## Problem

Parsing and signing a challenge is not the feature. The feature is a full, explainable paid-egress state machine that survives streaming, cancellation, duplicate retries, provider errors, and ambiguous settlement without bypassing the existing agent capability boundary.

## Scope and ownership

Wire one narrow production path: an already-governed managed/self-hosted external REST action pays an allowlisted x402 V2 Solana `exact` challenge.

- Keep the first unpaid dispatch and paid replay inside the same external-action execution context.
- Permit at most one payment negotiation/replay for the MVP. A second 402 is a typed failure, not a loop.
- Feed the `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` settlement evidence into the durable attempt state machine.
- Settle the wallet reservation only after valid durable success evidence.
- Definitive pre-submit failures release. Post-submit timeouts, cancellation, malformed/missing settlement evidence, or contradictory merchant response become `outcome_unknown` and enter bounded reconciliation.
- Preserve response streaming/backpressure and cancellation. Never buffer an unbounded paid response just to inspect headers.
- Extend runtime audit, request log, billing attribution, metrics, and trace fields without logging proofs or keys.

## Reconciliation

Define an injected settlement verifier/reconciler with bounded timeout/backoff and an explicit trust order (on-chain RPC/facilitator evidence versus merchant header). No external call occurs inside a database transaction. Unknown attempts remain visible and retain their holds until the verifier reaches a definitive result or an operator takes an audited override action.

## E2E closure for this slice

- **Operator input:** agent executes one allowlisted paid REST action under a configured spend policy.
- **Execution:** 402 -> authorize/reserve -> tenant-side sign -> exact replay -> validate settlement -> capture hold -> return resource.
- **Failure behavior:** denial and definite failure do not call the paid origin; unknown does not release or claim success; duplicate execution does not pay twice.
- **Evidence:** one trace links external action, policy revision, challenge/attempt/hold, worker, merchant, network/mint/atomic amount, transaction, and wallet settlement.
- **Regression:** local deterministic origin/facilitator doubles cover the full transition table, concurrency, cancellation, and streaming.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Happy path produces exactly one origin side effect, one on-chain settlement evidence record, and one internal wallet capture.
- [ ] Policy denial/insufficient funds never invokes signer or paid replay.
- [ ] Duplicate request/idempotency replay cannot sign, settle, or capture twice.
- [ ] Merchant returning 5xx after settlement, missing/invalid `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`, timeout after submit, client cancellation, and process restart all land in the documented state without silent loss.
- [ ] Reconciliation converges settled/not-submitted outcomes idempotently; unresolved attempts remain operator-visible with metrics and hold age.
- [ ] Existing egress allowlist, redirect, DNS/private-IP, response-size, timeout, and capability-boundary tests remain green.
- [ ] Admin audit/API answers "why was this payment made and what happened to it?" from durable evidence, not log scraping.
- [ ] Streaming tests prove bounded memory and correct cancellation/backpressure behavior.

## Verification

Focused async integration tests plus the narrow cross-component chain command added by this slice; static gates; clippy; no hosted Supabase or mainnet performance tests.

> **Scope note (rescoped 2026-07-30, closing the third code-review pass).**
> This issue delivers the **worker-side half only**: non-custodial 402 detection
> plus the *contract surface* for the spend-authorization handoff. The handoff
> types (`SpendAuthorizationRequest`, `AuthorizedHandoff`, `authorize_spend`,
> `sign_via`) are exactly that — a contract surface awaiting its caller, which
> lands in **#381**. They have no production caller in this repository today,
> which is why `x402_client.rs` still carries
> `#![cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]`. That attribute comes off when
> #381 wires the caller, not here.
>
> The gateway-minted `SpendAuthorization` token, the exact-once paid replay, and
> the durable attempt/hold integration have **moved to #381** (see *Scope
> correction* below). Do not gate this issue on them.

## Problem

The tenant's Solana key cannot live in FerroGate's gateway process or control-plane database. At the same time, a worker must not auto-pay any arbitrary 402 it sees. The signer needs a short-lived, cryptographically bound authorization from FerroGate before pay.sh/pay-kit can create an x402 proof.

## Scope correction — what moved to #381, and why it had to

The original acceptance list assumed one issue could deliver both ends of a
gateway-mediated boundary. It cannot, and the reason is structural rather than a
matter of effort:

- **`agent-worker` cannot reach the durable attempt API.** That API is
  `X402SettlementLoop` (`crates/ferrogate-gateway/src/state_x402_settlement.rs`:
  `open` / `submit` / `finalize` / `cancel` / `expire_if_due`) over
  `ferrogate_storage::RuntimeStorageRepositories`. `agent-worker/Cargo.toml`
  depends on `ferrogate-payments`, `ferrogate-policy` and `ferrogate-runtime` —
  and on neither `ferrogate-gateway` nor `ferrogate-storage`. Handing the worker
  a durable ledger handle would breach the very non-custody boundary this issue
  exists to protect, so the dependency is deliberately absent and must stay
  absent.
- **There is no gateway→worker `SpendAuthorization` transport to version.**
  `X402_VERSION` versions the *merchant* wire (#350), not this one. A token that
  does not exist cannot be bound, expired, replay-checked, or denied.
- **`agent-worker` has no live egress executor.** `run_authorized_rest_action`
  is a loopback smoke executor by construction: `parse_local_http_url` requires
  the authority to parse as a literal `SocketAddr` and refuses anything that is
  not `http://` and not loopback, and the dispatcher refuses any method but
  `GET`. An x402 merchant is a public DNS name over HTTPS, so no merchant can
  ever be on the other side of it.

Accordingly the following obligations are **removed from this issue and owned by
#381**:

- Versioned managed/self-hosted `SpendAuthorization` transport contracts that
  reject unknown/partial fields (former box 1).
- Denial of authorization replay, changed body, redirect, wrong worker, wrong
  recipient, larger amount, different mint/network, and expired token before
  signing (former box 3). All three of replay, expiry and worker-identity
  denial require the gateway-minted token above.
- The **gateway half** of cancellation: releasing through the durable attempt
  API before submission, and reporting `outcome_unknown` after it (former box 5).

## Scope and ownership (this issue)

- `agent-worker` / self-hosted worker: detect a 402 on an already-authorized REST egress action, parse it through the pay.sh adapter, and surface the challenge as a typed, fail-closed refusal. Own the one fact only the worker can observe — how far the request got on the wire — and emit it as a typed discriminant.
- `ferrogate-runtime`: `RequestWireStage` / `HoldDisposition` vocabulary, shared by both sides because both already depend on this crate.
- `ferrogate-payments`: injected signer trait (`SvmTransferSigner`) and pay.sh/pay-kit proof builder. Key loading remains outside core domain logic.

`ferrogate-cli`'s authenticated spend-authorization endpoint is **not** in this
issue; it belongs with #381's caller.

## Non-custodial boundary

- No private key, seed phrase, raw signing key, or recoverable key material crosses the gateway API.
- No key material enters config serialization, Postgres, traces, audit messages, panic output, or Debug implementations.
- A self-hosted worker can supply its own signer. Managed-worker production signing requires an explicit external signer/KMS boundary, not an env-var shortcut silently promoted to production.
- Human approval remains possible above a policy threshold. No headless auto-pay unless policy explicitly allows it.

## Security cases (this issue)

Refuse proof creation if URL/method/body, challenge, recipient, amount, mint, network, worker identity, or expiry differs from the authorization. Refuse when the merchant supplies more than one `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header, because two challenges are two spend demands and picking either one reports evidence the merchant did not unambiguously make. Strip merchant-supplied internal authorization headers. Preserve existing DNS/private-network/allowlist checks.

Re-authorization after redirects and non-carriage of a proof across origins are
part of the replay path and move to **#381** with it.

## E2E closure for this slice

- **Operator input:** a fake local x402 peer answering `402` on the worker's authorized egress action.
- **Execution:** the worker detects the challenge, validates it against the frozen wire contract, proves it is not redirecting payment away from the authorized URL, and refuses — exactly once, with no replay.
- **Evidence:** the refusal names only public challenge evidence (challenge hash, network, atomic amount, recipient); proof and credential material are redacted before truncation; the wire stage reaches the gateway as a frozen token rather than a substring match.
- **Regression:** a fake local x402 peer and a fake signer prove every binding mismatch without real funds.

The paid-replay half of this closure (authorization, signing, single replay,
settlement evidence) moves to **#381**.

## Acceptance

- [x] Signer is dependency-injected (`SvmTransferSigner`); the gateway never receives private key bytes. **Zeroization is vacuous here and stays vacuous until #381:** the trait has zero production implementations in the repository — every impl is in a test file — so there is no production key material in this crate to zeroize. The zeroization/isolation obligation attaches to the first real signer backend, which is #381's to add.
- [x] Proof/payment headers are never logged and are removed before responses are exposed to an untrusted model; redaction precedes truncation, and the two public protocol headers (`PAYMENT-REQUIRED`, `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`) are deliberately preserved so the audit trail survives.
- [x] Non-custodial 402 detection fails closed on every failure mode: a missing challenge header, **duplicate challenge headers**, an unparseable challenge, and a challenge whose protected resource is not the authorized egress URL. None of them pays, and none replays.
- [x] The wire stage the worker observes is emitted as a typed discriminant (`ferrogate_runtime::EGRESS_REQUEST_WIRE_STAGE_KEY`), with the fail-safe direction — retain the hold unless the request is *proven* unsent — surviving the management wire in both directions.
- [x] Focused async tests use barriers/channels, not sleeps, for authorization/replay races.

### Moved to #381 (do not gate this issue on these)

- [ ] Managed and self-hosted `SpendAuthorization` transport contracts are versioned and reject unknown/partial fields. → **#381**
- [ ] Authorization replay, changed body, redirect, wrong worker, wrong recipient, larger amount, different mint/network, and expired token are denied before signing. → **#381**
- [ ] Cancellation before submission releases through the durable attempt API; cancellation after submission reports unknown. → **#381**
- [ ] Removal of `#![cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` from `x402_client.rs`, once the handoff types have a production caller. → **#381**

## Known gap, disclosed rather than closed

Every x402 test builds its own `CannedOrigin`, so the smoke command is not what
makes them run; they prove the functions are correct, not that they ship on a
live path. That is a consequence of the missing egress executor above, not an
oversight, and it closes when #381 provides one.

The worker's 402 header/requirement selection and the gateway's are still two
implementations with no shared conformance fixture. This is a **factoring
choice, not an impossibility**: `crates/agent-worker/Cargo.toml:25` and
`crates/ferrogate-gateway/Cargo.toml:50` both depend on `ferrogate-payments`, so
the shared decision can be hoisted there and driven from one fixture set — the
same move already made for `RequestWireStage` into `ferrogate-runtime`. Filed as
a hoist, not as an impossibility: **#593**.

## Verification

Focused `agent-worker`, `ferrogate-runtime` and `ferrogate-payments` tests; clippy with all targets/features; secret-redaction assertions; no mainnet invocation.

body:
Parent: #349 · Depends on #281 and #351

## Problem

A wallet hold alone cannot explain or reconcile an on-chain payment. FerroGate needs a durable payment-attempt identity and an explicit truth table for crashes and timeouts. Releasing a hold because a post-submit HTTP request timed out can spend stablecoin without charging the internal wallet; blindly settling can double-charge a failed payment.

## Scope and ownership

- `ferrogate-storage`: repository contract and in-memory/Postgres implementation for immutable payment intent fields plus state transitions.
- `ferrogate-payments`: state/transition types only; no SQL.
- `ferrogate-cli`: narrow Admin API to list/get attempts and inspect linked wallet reservation/settlement.

Proposed states: `challenged -> authorized -> submitted -> settled`, with terminal `denied`, `released`, `failed`, plus non-terminal `outcome_unknown`. Exact names may change, but their semantics may not.

Persist at minimum: attempt/idempotency ID, tenant/project/workspace/run/worker/request IDs, method and canonical resource, request-body hash, challenge hash, x402 version/scheme, CAIP-2 network, asset mint, atomic amount, recipient, conversion snapshot, policy revision/decision, hold ID, submission time, transaction signature/settlement response, failure code, and timestamps.

## Mutation truth table

- Before proof submission, a definitive denial/cancel/expiry may release the hold.
- After submission, timeout/cancellation/RPC ambiguity is `outcome_unknown`; it must retain the hold until durable evidence proves settled or not submitted.
- `settled` captures exactly one existing active hold and records the transaction signature.
- Replaying the same transition is idempotent. A conflicting challenge or transaction under the same idempotency ID fails closed.
- A stale reread while a mutation is unresolved is not proof of failure. Preserve operation generation/version through the storage scheduler.

## E2E closure for this slice

- **Operator input:** create an authorization for a validated payment intent.
- **Execution:** one conditional durable transition creates the attempt and reserves wallet credits; later simulated evidence settles, releases, or marks unknown.
- **Evidence:** Admin API joins attempt, hold, wallet settlement, policy revision, and transaction evidence.
- **Regression:** deterministic barrier/channel concurrency and crash-point tests prove no oversell, double capture, or silent release.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Repository contracts and migrations preserve the complete audit tuple and enforce tenant ownership.
- [ ] The result truth table explicitly covers pre-commit cancellation, CommitInFlight, OutcomeUnknown, duplicate transition, conflict, expiry, and late settlement.
- [ ] N concurrent authorizations against funds for N-1 result in exactly N-1 durable attempts/holds.
- [ ] Duplicate settled evidence captures once; conflicting transaction evidence fails closed and emits an operator-visible error.
- [ ] A timeout after submission leaves an inspectable unknown attempt and active hold; it is not reported as failed/released.
- [ ] Reads are indexed, tenant-scoped before pagination, and use no blocking Postgres bridge in the hot path.
- [ ] Database work is short conditional CRUD/CAS. Any transaction requires a written irreducible-invariant justification and contains no external call/wait/retry.
- [ ] Postgres restart/durability coverage proves attempts and links survive restart.

## Verification

Focused `ferrogate-storage` tests, `ferrogate-test postgres-restart` coverage for payment attempts, OpenAPI check, clippy, and migration/schema validation.

body:
Parent: #349 · Depends on #350

## Problem

An x402 challenge is untrusted merchant input. pay.sh can enforce a local amount cap and network pin, but FerroGate needs tenant/project/workspace/key and agent-run policy: which resource, recipient, mint, network, amount, and approval mode may be paid. Internal wallet credits and Solana token atomic units are different money domains and cannot be bridged with an ad hoc `f64` conversion.

## Scope and ownership

- `ferrogate-payments`: immutable `PaymentIntent` and integer money types. Required fields: protocol/version, scheme, CAIP-2 network, asset mint, atomic amount, recipient, resource URL, HTTP method, request-body hash, challenge hash, merchant timeout, tenant/workspace/run/worker/request identity.
- `ferrogate-config`: typed, disabled-by-default x402 config with allowlisted network + canonical USDC mint, resource/payee rules, per-payment/per-run/time-window caps, approval threshold/mode, and conversion rule/version.
- `ferrogate-policy`: pure `AgentSpendPolicy` evaluation returning Allow, Deny, or ApprovalRequired with stable reason codes and a conversion snapshot. No signer or storage calls inside policy.
- Admin/config visibility must expose the effective policy and its revision without exposing signer material.

MVP accepts x402 V2 `exact` on explicit Solana sandbox/devnet configuration. A mainnet network/mint pair requires an explicit production config and must never be inferred from a token symbol such as `USDC`.

## Security invariants

- Match canonicalized HTTPS resource origin/path and exact recipient. Do not trust challenge display text or token symbol.
- Bind policy to the already-authorized egress request. A challenge cannot redirect payment to another URL, body, recipient, or network.
- All amount math is checked integer/rational arithmetic with a persisted conversion snapshot. Overflow or missing/expired conversion data denies.
- Default action for unknown scheme/network/mint/payee, ambiguous accepts entries, or amount over cap is Deny.

## E2E closure for this slice

- **Operator input:** typed config/API policy for one tenant and one allowed Solana devnet USDC merchant.
- **Execution:** the same payment intent is evaluated at tenant/project/workspace/key/run scope and produces an explicit decision plus conversion snapshot.
- **Evidence:** decision contains policy revision, matched rule, reason code, original atomic units, computed internal credits, and challenge hash.
- **Regression:** allow, deny, and approval-required cases prove the config written is what runtime policy reads.

## Acceptance

- [ ] No money field uses `f32`/`f64`; serialization preserves atomic amounts losslessly.
- [ ] Config validation rejects wildcard mainnet, token-symbol-only allowlists, HTTP resources (except explicit local test mode), negative/zero caps, duplicate rules, and impossible conversion ratios.
- [ ] Policy precedence and scope inheritance are deterministic and tested across tenant/project/workspace/key plus agent run.
- [ ] Property tests cover monotonic caps, overflow, round-up/round-down behavior, and "raising quoted amount can never turn Deny into Allow".
- [ ] Effective-policy Admin API/config diagnostics expose decisions and revisions but no secret/signer fields.
- [ ] OpenAPI/config examples and schema checks are updated for the same fields runtime consumes.

## Verification

`cargo +1.88.0 test -p ferrogate-config -p ferrogate-policy -p ferrogate-payments --all-features`, focused property tests, `python3 scripts/check-openapi.py`, and `cargo +1.88.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.

body:
Parent: #349 · Refs #191 and #281

## Problem

pay.sh is the preferred Solana x402 implementation, but dependency shape and wire behavior must be proven before it enters FerroGate's runtime. The current official material is not one stable surface:

- pay.sh documents `solana-pay-kit` as the Rust SDK and crates.io currently resolves 0.2.0.
- the pay CLI source pins a specific `pay-kit` git revision and enables a much broader feature set than FerroGate needs.
- the documented Rust paying-client guide is MPP-centric even though the crate and pay CLI expose x402 client code.

Blindly adding the whole SDK, axum middleware, or a `pay` subprocess to each request would be bad architecture.

## Scope and ownership

Create a narrow, protocol-neutral crate boundary, proposed as `crates/ferrogate-payments`, and qualify the smallest pay.sh/pay-kit surface needed for **x402 V2 + Solana SVM + exact + client**.

- Define adapter contracts for parsing a payment challenge, selecting one supported requirement, building a proof through an injected signer, and decoding settlement evidence.
- Keep HTTP dispatch, policy, wallet storage, and key loading outside the crate.
- Compile with minimal features. Do not enable axum/server, MPP, subscriptions, confidential transfer, OTEL, or testkit unless evidence shows a required path.
- Add checked-in golden fixtures from the x402 V2 HTTP/SVM specs for `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`, `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`, and `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`.
- Document version pinning, MSRV/toolchain compatibility, license, dependency/SBOM impact, and upgrade policy.

## Failure contract

Typed errors must distinguish: malformed/oversized header, unsupported x402 version, no acceptable requirement, unsupported network/scheme/mint, invalid atomic amount, invalid recipient, expired/unsafe timeout, signer rejected, proof build failed, settlement header malformed, and SDK incompatibility. Never turn an invalid amount into zero.

## E2E closure for this slice

- **Operator input:** a checked-in canonical Solana x402 V2 challenge fixture and a sandbox-only test signer.
- **Execution:** FerroGate parses, validates, selects, and builds a proof through the pay.sh adapter without starting Pingora or touching mainnet.
- **Evidence:** structured adapter result includes network, mint, atomic amount, recipient, resource, expiry, and deterministic challenge hash; secret bytes are absent from Debug/serde output.
- **Regression:** golden round-trip and negative corpus tests run offline; an opt-in compatibility smoke test may run against `pay --sandbox server`, never as the only proof.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `cargo metadata --locked` resolves on the workspace toolchain and aarch64; the exact crate version/revision and enabled features are recorded.
- [ ] `cargo tree -p ferrogate-payments` shows no accidental axum/server or broad pay CLI dependency.
- [ ] Golden tests cover x402 V2 HTTP headers and Solana CAIP-2 IDs, including mainnet/devnet recognition while tests remain local/sandbox.
- [ ] Fuzz/property-style negative cases reject malformed base64/JSON, overflow, zero/negative/non-integer amounts, duplicate/conflicting accepts entries, and oversized headers without panic.
- [ ] License/SBOM and `cargo deny check` / `cargo audit` results are recorded; unresolved security or source-availability risk blocks runtime wiring.
- [ ] No production route, wallet mutation, signer key loading, or mainnet call is added in this issue.

## Verification

`cargo +1.88.0 test -p ferrogate-payments --all-features` (plus a minimal-feature build), `cargo +1.88.0 clippy -p ferrogate-payments --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo metadata --locked --format-version=1`, and `git diff --check`.

body:
Parent: #268

## Decision

Add Solana x402 as an **agent-payment rail**, not as another implementation of the existing Stripe top-up adapter.

The first product path is outbound paid egress: a FerroGate-managed or self-hosted agent encounters an x402 V2 challenge, FerroGate authorizes the exact spend against tenant policy and an existing wallet reservation, and the tenant-side worker/signing backend uses pay.sh / `solana-pay-kit` to create the payment proof. FerroGate records and reconciles the outcome but never stores a tenant Solana private key.

Inbound monetization of FerroGate APIs is useful, but it is a separate P2 sidecar slice. It must not be mixed into the outbound authorization state machine.

## Why this shape

- #191 already concluded GO for authorize + audit, never custody.
- #281 shipped the durable wallet `reserve -> settle|release` prerequisite.
- pay.sh officially supports x402/MPP through `pay server` and `solana-pay-kit`; its CLI is a process/tool surface, not something to spawn once per gateway request.
- The Rust SDK's server helper is axum-specific. FerroGate is Pingora-based, so axum middleware does not belong in the request hot path.
- The existing `PaymentProviderAdapter` in `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/payments.rs` is for collecting fiat top-ups from a customer. Reusing it for an agent's outbound stablecoin spend would conflate opposite money flows and incompatible idempotency/settlement semantics.

## Target architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Agent/worker
    participant R as Paid API
    participant G as FerroGate authorization
    participant W as Wallet reservation store
    participant S as Tenant-side signer/pay.sh

    A->>R: Original governed HTTP request
    R-->>A: 402 + PAYMENT-REQUIRED
    A->>G: Bound payment intent + challenge hash
    G->>G: Egress + spend policy evaluation
    G->>W: Reserve exact internal credits
    W-->>G: hold_id
    G-->>A: Short-lived spend authorization
    A->>S: Sign exact x402 payload locally
    S-->>A: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
    A->>R: Replay exact request + proof
    R-->>A: Response + PAYMENT-RESPONSE
    A->>G: Settlement evidence or explicit unknown
    G->>W: Settle, release, or retain hold for reconciliation
```

## MVP invariants

1. Disabled by default. No challenge is auto-paid without explicit tenant policy.
2. x402 V2 `exact` only. Start with Solana sandbox/devnet and explicitly allowlisted USDC mint(s); mainnet is a later operator choice, never a test default.
3. Money is integer atomic units. Persist `network`, asset mint, amount, recipient, resource, challenge hash, conversion snapshot, and hold ID. No `f64` in authorization or settlement.
4. Bind authorization to tenant/run/worker, HTTP method, canonical URL, request-body hash, challenge hash, recipient, asset, amount, network, and expiry. Redirects or a changed retry invalidate it.
5. Tenant key material stays in the tenant-controlled worker, OS key store, or remote signer/KMS. It is never stored in FerroGate config, Postgres, logs, audit events, or traces.
6. Wallet capture happens only on durable settlement evidence. Definitive pre-submit failure releases the hold. Timeout after submission is `outcome_unknown`, not failure, until reconciled.
7. The paid egress path remains behind the existing capability/egress boundary. x402 must not become an SSRF, redirect, DNS-rebinding, or arbitrary-payee bypass.
8. Every authorization and settlement decision emits inspectable request/run/tenant/hold/payment-attempt attribution.

## Out of scope for the P1 chain

- AP2 mandates.
- EVM/Base support.
- MPP negotiation, subscriptions, `upto`, and batch settlement.
- FerroGate-operated custodial wallets.
- Mainnet load/performance tests.
- Replacing Stripe wallet top-ups.

## Primary references

- Existing FerroGate spike: `docs/design/x402-ap2-spike-2026-07.md` (#191)
- Existing hold primitive: #281
- pay.sh docs: https://pay.sh/docs and https://pay.sh/docs/sdk/rust
- pay.sh source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/pay
- x402 V2 spec: https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/main/specs/x402-specification-v2.md
- x402 HTTP V2 transport: https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/main/specs/transports-v2/http.md

## Epic acceptance

- [ ] A managed or self-hosted worker can pay one allowlisted Solana x402 V2 `exact` challenge in a no-mainnet-funds environment.
- [ ] Policy denial, insufficient wallet balance, unsupported network/mint, changed recipient/URL/body, expired challenge, malformed proof, duplicate replay, and timeout-after-submit are fail-closed and covered.
- [ ] A settled transaction captures exactly one wallet hold; a definitive pre-submit failure releases it; an unknown outcome cannot silently release or double-charge.
- [ ] Admin/API evidence answers: who authorized the spend, for which agent/run/request, to which recipient/resource, for how much, using which asset/network, with which hold and on-chain transaction.
- [ ] `ferrogate-test` has component-compliance and cross-component scenarios, with no performance/load traffic against hosted pay.sh/Surfpool or mainnet.

Scope is only the attached sub-issues. Keep this epic open until the P1 chain is complete; the P2 inbound monetization child is independently closable.


## Execution order

1. #350 qualifies and freezes the pay.sh / `solana-pay-kit` x402 SVM contract. This is the only child initially Ready.
2. #351 defines immutable integer money/payment-intent types and tenant-scoped spend policy.
3. #352 persists payment attempts and couples their state machine to the already-shipped #281 wallet hold.
4. #353 adds the non-custodial worker-side signer handoff. Private keys never enter the gateway.
5. #354 wires the one-replay paid-egress runtime loop and outcome-unknown reconciliation.
6. #355 proves write-path == runtime-read-path with component compliance and a no-mainnet-funds cross-component E2E.
7. #356 is an independent P2 experiment for inbound fixed-price monetization through a pay.sh sidecar. It does not block the outbound P1 chain.

Dependency DAG: `#350 -> #351 -> #352 -> #353 -> #354 -> #355`; #353 also directly depends on #350/#351, and #356 depends only on #350.

Parent: #295.
Depends on: #346.
Related: #313, #331, #334, #337-#345.

Origin: operator request on 2026-07-21.

## Problem

#346 establishes the i18n runtime, but the product requirement is not complete until every operator-facing Admin Console workflow is usable in English and Simplified Chinese. The current console spans auth, shell/navigation, generated resource CRUD, agent/MCP/worker operations, guardrails/evidence, billing, system operations, assets, and static-site management. Partial translation would leave mixed-language workflows and inaccessible labels.

## Scope

- Migrate all operator-facing copy to the typed `en` and `zh-CN` catalogs:
  - login/register/session errors and protected shell/navigation/breadcrumbs;
  - dashboard, overview alerts, and shared loading/empty/stale/error states;
  - generated resource titles, descriptions, columns, fields, options, validation, dialogs, pagination, and row actions;
  - tenancy/IAM/billing, routing/policy/quota/guardrail, agent/MCP/worker/operations forms from #340-#342;
  - assets/static-site/domain flows from #344-#345;
  - toasts, confirmations, tooltips, accessible names, skip links, and route-load failures.
- Use semantic keys and interpolation/plural rules. Do not concatenate translated fragments or use English text as a key.
- Localize dates, times, relative times, numbers, tokens, bytes, percentages, and currencies through #346 formatters.
- Keep FerroGate, provider/model names, API paths, identifiers, hashes, code/config values, user content, and raw technical evidence unchanged and protected from browser auto-translation where appropriate.
- Review Chinese terminology for consistent control-plane vocabulary; maintain a small glossary for tenant/project/workspace, provider/model, policy/guardrail, tokens/cost, MCP, agent run, worker, asset, and deployment terms.
- Test both locales at 390x844, 768x1024, and 1440x900. Fix wrapping/truncation/overflow caused by either catalog without locale-specific fixed widths.
- Add a lint/static inventory that rejects newly introduced hard-coded operator strings outside an explicit reviewed allowlist.
- Update contributor documentation with key naming, namespace ownership, glossary, and the procedure for adding a locale.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every registered route is covered by the English/Chinese browser route matrix with no mixed-language shell or primary workflow.
- [ ] Every visible command, field label, option, validation/error, status, confirmation, tooltip, toast, and accessible name has both catalog entries.
- [ ] Generated resource CRUD and bespoke pages use the same typed catalog contract; no CSV/JSON/resource metadata text is silently skipped.
- [ ] English and Chinese render without overlapping controls, clipped primary actions, or document-level horizontal overflow at the 3 required viewports.
- [ ] Dates, numbers, token counts, bytes, percentages, relative times, and currencies are locale-correct and tested.
- [ ] Identifiers/code/user content remain byte-for-byte unchanged when switching locale.
- [ ] Missing keys fail the local gate; unknown backend errors fall back to localized generic copy plus unchanged technical detail.
- [ ] Playwright covers auth, dashboard, generic CRUD, one relationship form, guardrail/evidence, agent/worker, billing/ops, asset/site, dialogs, and mobile navigation in both locales.

## Non-goals

- Additional locales beyond `en` and `zh-CN`.
- Translating API payloads, audit evidence, user-generated content, provider output, or source-code examples.
- A content-management system for translations.

Parent: #295.
Related: #331, #334.

Origin: operator request on 2026-07-21.

## Problem

The console already depends on `next-themes` and defines light/dark CSS variables in `admin-console/src/index.css`, but `App` has no `ThemeProvider` and the shell has no theme control. The dark tokens therefore are not a complete operator-facing feature, and `Toaster` reads a theme context that is never configured.

A control-plane UI is used for long sessions and incident response. Theme behavior must be global, persistent, accessible, and verified across every shared surface rather than implemented as a page-local color toggle.

## Scope

- Add one root theme provider using the existing `next-themes` dependency and class-based Tailwind dark mode.
- Support Light, Dark, and System. Default to System for a first visit; persist an explicit operator choice in a versioned/minimal browser preference.
- Add an accessible global theme control in the protected shell and an equivalent reachable control on auth pages. Use familiar sun/moon/system icons with labels/tooltips; do not require a page reload.
- Apply the resolved theme before first paint so login, direct deep links, and reload do not flash the wrong background.
- Keep `<html>` `color-scheme` and `<meta name="theme-color">` synchronized with the resolved theme so native controls, scrollbars, browser chrome, dialogs, selects, and toasts match.
- Audit semantic tokens and one-off status colors across shell, auth, dashboard, tables, forms, charts/metrics, badges, code blocks, dialogs/sheets, destructive states, focus rings, and Sonner toasts. Remove hard-coded colors that become unreadable in either theme.
- React to operating-system theme changes only while System is selected.
- Preserve the current route, unsaved form state, sidebar state, and focus when changing theme.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Light, Dark, and System can be selected globally from keyboard, pointer, and assistive technology without navigation or reload.
- [ ] Explicit selection survives reload/direct deep link; System follows `prefers-color-scheme` changes.
- [ ] No visible wrong-theme flash occurs on login or representative protected deep links.
- [ ] `html` color scheme, browser theme color, native selects/inputs, dialogs, and toasts match the resolved theme.
- [ ] Representative auth, dashboard, resource table/form, billing/ops, and modal routes have zero axe critical/serious color-contrast failures in light and dark modes.
- [ ] Focus, hover, active, disabled, success, warning, and destructive states remain distinguishable in both themes.
- [ ] Vitest covers preference resolution/persistence; Playwright covers light/dark/system, reload, OS-change emulation, mobile, and screenshots.
- [ ] The change does not add another theming dependency.

## Non-goals

- User-defined colors or tenant branding.
- Persisting theme in the control-plane database.

Parent: #295.

Origin: operator request on 2026-07-21.

## Problem

The Admin Console has no localization runtime. Navigation, route titles, resource metadata, forms, validation, status text, toasts, accessible names, and date/number/currency formatting are hard-coded in English. Adding scattered language conditionals would create an untestable second copy of the UI.

## Decision

Use a mature React i18n runtime (recommended: `i18next` + `react-i18next`) with typed translation keys and route-level namespaces. A small dedicated dependency is justified here; do not build a custom translation map/provider.

Canonical initial locales are `en` and `zh-CN`.

## Scope

- Add one app-level i18n provider with English as the source/fallback locale and Simplified Chinese as the second locale.
- Resolve initial locale in this order: valid persisted choice, `navigator.languages`, then English. Do not infer language from IP.
- Add an accessible global language selector to auth pages and the protected shell. Switching locale must not reload or reset route/form/sidebar state.
- Persist only a validated locale code in a versioned/minimal browser preference and update `<html lang>` immediately.
- Establish typed keys, interpolation, pluralization, and route-level namespaces compatible with existing lazy routes. Load only the active locale/namespace; do not put every page's two catalogs in the initial bundle.
- Add shared locale-aware formatters using `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, and currency formatting. Remove locale-implicit `toLocaleString()` helpers as pages migrate.
- Make navigation/resource configuration carry translation keys rather than translated strings, including field labels, descriptions, placeholders, enum labels, column headers, row actions, and breadcrumbs. Coordinate this contract with #337.
- Define stable mappings from backend error/status codes to localized operator copy while retaining unknown server details as clearly marked technical detail. Do not try to translate identifiers, code, provider/model names, or user content.
- Add missing-key, fallback, interpolation, namespace-load, and locale-format tests plus a catalog consistency check in the local admin-console gate.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `en` and `zh-CN` are selectable before and after authentication without a full document reload.
- [ ] Locale survives reload/direct deep link, updates `html[lang]`, and falls back safely for invalid/missing preferences.
- [ ] Lazy routes load only the active locale namespace and do not duplicate the full translation catalog in the initial bundle.
- [ ] Translation keys are type-checked and CI/local checks reject missing English keys, missing Chinese keys, and accidental key drift.
- [ ] Shared date, time, number, token, byte, percentage, relative-time, and currency formatters produce locale-correct output.
- [ ] Backend identifiers and unknown error detail remain intact and are marked `translate="no"` where appropriate.
- [ ] Unit tests cover detection/persistence/fallback/pluralization/formatting; Playwright covers language switching on auth and one protected route.
- [ ] Before/after bundle output is recorded and remains inside the existing budget.

## Non-goals

- Translating every page in this foundation issue.
- Server-side localization of Admin API payloads.
- Machine-translating operator or user-provided content.

Parent: #295.
Depends on: #337, #338.
Related: #258, #265, #323.

Origin: operator review of static-resource management on 2026-07-21.

## Problem

Static sites are technically publishable as `static_site` ZIP assets and servable under `/sites/{tenant}/{site}/...`, and custom domains have a separate bind page. The console has no coherent site-management module: operators must know the ZIP convention, type special headers/paths indirectly, infer the serve URL, and jump to a domain form that asks for tenant/site strings.

## Scope

- Add a Static sites view that lists logical sites with tenant, bundle version, public/private state, SPA fallback, cache policy, file count/bytes, publish time, serve URL, and bound domains.
- Add a publish/republish flow for a ZIP bundle with explicit tenant/project/site selection, bundle version, public/private, SPA fallback, and cache-control controls.
- Validate archive type/size client-side for fast feedback while preserving authoritative gateway validation and displaying scan/zip-bomb/quota failures verbatim and accessibly.
- Show upload/publish progress and a publish result containing the canonical serve URL; never claim deployment before the gateway commits the site manifest/files.
- Provide safe preview/open actions and a deployment/history surface based only on durable versions/audit evidence the API exposes.
- Integrate custom-domain binding/unbinding into the site context using entity pickers; keep ACME posture and reload result visible.
- Define the static-site bundle headers/result in the enforced OpenAPI/generated client as part of #338 if absent.
- Preserve tenant/site/version selection in the URL and support direct links.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An operator can publish a valid ZIP and open its canonical `/sites/{tenant}/{site}/` URL without knowing the raw asset route.
- [ ] Public/private, SPA fallback, cache policy, version, files, bytes, and publish timestamp are visible and match the committed manifest.
- [ ] Republish failure leaves the previous committed site usable and the UI states the actual outcome.
- [ ] Tenant and published-site selection uses #337 controls; domain binding cannot target a nonexistent or cross-tenant site.
- [ ] Bound domains and ACME status are visible from the site detail, with confirmed unbind.
- [ ] Invalid archive, quota exceeded, scan rejection, partial upload, and backend unavailable states are tested.
- [ ] Playwright covers publish, republish, open/preview, bind/unbind, mobile, and keyboard behavior.

## Non-goals

- A WYSIWYG website builder.
- Fabricating deployment history when the backend has no durable evidence; any missing history contract must be filed explicitly.

body:
Parent: #295.
Depends on: #338.
Related: #178, #260, #336.

Origin: operator review of `/app/assets` on 2026-07-21.

## Problem

An Assets route exists, but it is only a thin single-file push/list/download/delete screen. It does not provide actual lifecycle management for the five supported static resource types: CLI tools, MCP manifests, skill bundles, static sites, and config files.

It cannot browse logical packages, inspect manifests/variants, move channels, yank/unyank versions, use the large-object presigned path, or safely explain destructive operations. It computes quota usage by summing the current list page and deletes immediately without confirmation.

## Scope

- Rebuild the route as a registry: type/search/filter list of logical resources, then a detail view for manifest, versions, variants, hashes, storage backend, timestamps, and channels.
- Support channel create/move/delete and version yank/unyank with explicit consequences and audit-aware confirmation.
- Keep permanent version deletion separate from yank and require destructive confirmation that names the exact resource/version and reports channel/reference blockers.
- Add inline vs presigned upload selection based on file size/backend capability, with checksum, progress, cancellation, commit, retryable failure state, and no false success before commit.
- Use authoritative storage bytes/quota from #338 and expose quota pressure without client-side list summation.
- Provide typed download for inline and bucket-backed versions, copyable install/pull references, and clear scan/signature/trust status only where the API has evidence.
- Preserve type, search, filters, selected resource, and version in the URL.
- Make tables/detail panels responsive and reuse the browser gate from #331/#336.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All supported asset types can be searched and managed without entering route paths or raw asset IDs.
- [ ] A logical resource detail shows versions, variants, yank state, channels, hashes, sizes, and storage mode from the typed manifest.
- [ ] Operators can promote/rollback a channel and yank/unyank a version with confirmed, audited mutations.
- [ ] Large bucket-backed uploads complete the presign -> transfer -> commit path; cancellation/failure does not appear as published.
- [ ] Permanent delete is clearly distinct from yank, confirmed, and reports blockers/failure.
- [ ] Quota is authoritative, including paginated registries.
- [ ] Unit/query tests cover lifecycle mutations; Playwright covers upload, promotion, yank, download, delete confirmation, mobile, and partial errors.

## Non-goals

- Implementing missing scanner/signature evidence in the UI by inference.
- A static-site authoring editor; site publishing gets a focused workflow.

## Problem

#332 correctly replaced the 50-card route launcher, but the current dashboard still is not a global control-plane overview. It shows readiness, provider health, approvals, recent requests, and one latest usage report. It does not expose global total tokens, MCP servers, static assets/storage, agent runs, complete resource inventory, utilization/reference counts, or a prioritized error summary.

The current "Latest cost" and usage token value are period-report values; presenting them as global totals would be misleading.

## Scope

- Consume the typed `GET /admin/v1/overview` contract from #339. Do not fan out across every resource list or count a paginated page in the browser.
- Put global traffic/cost and core runtime counts in the first viewport: total tokens with an explicit period, requests/cost, MCP servers, static assets/storage, agent runs, and active workers.
- Add a scannable resource inventory grouped by control-plane domain, with total and meaningful utilization/reference/state breakdowns plus links to the filtered source pages.
- Add a prioritized alerts region for unhealthy providers, failed requests/runs, quota pressure, pending approvals, stale workers, and unavailable overview sections.
- Show scope, generated timestamp, freshness/staleness, and partial-data states. Never render unavailable data as zero.
- Keep the layout quiet and dense. Do not recreate one decorative card per navigation item; use stable summary bands/tables and progressive disclosure.
- Preserve overview filter/period state in the URL where user-selectable.
- Refresh with a bounded polling policy and pause/background-throttle appropriately.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The first desktop viewport answers resource size, traffic/cost, health, and urgent action without scrolling.
- [ ] Global token total is labeled with its exact scope/period and is not derived from the latest usage report.
- [ ] MCP server, static asset/storage, and agent-run counts link to their corresponding filtered management views.
- [ ] Resource utilization/reference values have labels that state their semantics; not-applicable and unavailable are distinct from zero.
- [ ] One failed overview section remains visible as a partial error and does not blank healthy sections.
- [ ] 390x844, 768x1024, and 1440x900 Playwright cases prove no overlap/overflow and preserve the same information priority.
- [ ] Query/component tests cover loading, empty, stale, partial failure, and polling cleanup.

## Non-goals
