body:
**Severity: High** · found while investigating Supabase schema isolation across the decomposed gateway/billing/auth services.

## Summary
The gateway's control-plane storage already has a documented, working dedicated-schema design (`postgres_schema: ferrogate_control` in `[storage]` config, see `docs/durable-storage.md`). The standalone `ferrogate billing serve` and `ferrogate auth serve` services (added by the service-decomposition work, epic #128) support the same underlying mechanism (`--supabase-schema` / `FERROGATE_BILLING_SUPABASE_SCHEMA` / `FERROGATE_AUTH_SUPABASE_SCHEMA`), but the flag has **no default value** on either service (`Option<String>`, `None` when unset) — and the same gap exists in the standalone `ferrogate-auth` binary's own duplicated CLI parsing.

When an operator points `ferrogate billing serve --supabase-dsn ...` or `ferrogate auth serve --supabase-dsn ...` at a Supabase project **without** explicitly also passing `--supabase-schema`, both services silently fall back to Postgres's default `public` schema. If the gateway's own control-plane connection (or another service) targets the same Supabase project, all of billing's, auth's, and the gateway's tables end up flattened into one shared `public` namespace with no isolation — defeating the purpose of running them as independently-deployable services and risking table-name collisions or accidental cross-service data visibility.

Compounding this, the `--supabase-schema` flag's help text on both services literally says *"Optional PostgreSQL schema containing the FerroGate control-plane tables"* — copy-pasted from the gateway's own wording, which is actively misleading (it should describe each service's own tables, not the gateway's).

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/cli.rs`: `BillingServeArgs.supabase_schema` (~line 219) and `AuthServeArgs.supabase_schema` (~line 163) are both `Option<String>` with no `default_value`.
- `crates/ferrogate-auth/src/main.rs`: `ServeArgs.supabase_schema` (line 49) — the standalone `ferrogate-auth` binary duplicates this same gap independently.
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/service_storage.rs::build_supabase_repositories`: when `connection.schema` is `None`, `PostgresStorageConfig.schema` is `None`, and `crates/ferrogate-storage/src/lib.rs`'s `SET search_path`/`CREATE SCHEMA` logic (~line 3563) is skipped entirely, leaving the session on Postgres's default `public` search path.
- `sql/001_init_postgres.sql`'s schema-creation/validation logic (`CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS {schema}; SET search_path TO {schema}, public;`) is already schema-name-agnostic — it works correctly for any schema name today (proven by the gateway's own `ferrogate_control` usage), so no migration-logic changes are needed, only the CLI-level defaulting.

## Suggested fix
Give `--supabase-schema` a sensible default on both services (`billing` for the billing service, `auth` for the auth service — mirroring the gateway's own `ferrogate_control` convention), in all three definition sites (`ferrogate-cli`'s `BillingServeArgs`/`AuthServeArgs`, and the standalone `ferrogate-auth` binary's own `ServeArgs`), and correct the misleading help text. Add Docker-based Supabase round-trip coverage proving billing and auth land their tables under their own dedicated schemas by default, with no explicit flag required, and that this doesn't collide with the gateway's own `ferrogate_control` schema against the same database.
title: [storage][high] billing/auth services default to the shared public Supabase schema instead of dedicated schemas

body:
**Severity: Low** · found while fixing README's Quick Start / the default `Ferrogate/Caddyfile` (unauthenticated-by-default gateway config).

## Summary
The TOML config format supports prefix-stripped reverse proxying via `[[upstreams]] name/url` + `[[routes]] name/upstream/path_prefixes/strip_prefix` (see `config/ferrogate.example.toml`'s `/proxy/httpbin` example). The Caddyfile format has no equivalent: `route`/`handle`/`handle_path` + `reverse_proxy` blocks (`crates/ferrogate-config/src/caddyfile/parser.rs`, `parse_reverse_proxy`) always leave `GatewayRoute.strip_prefix` as `None` — there is no directive anywhere in the Caddyfile grammar that sets it, and `handle_path` (which implies stripping in real Caddy) is dispatched identically to plain `route`/`handle` with no special-casing.

## Failure scenario
An operator writes a Caddyfile block like:
```caddyfile
route /proxy/httpbin/* {
    reverse_proxy https://httpbin.org
}
```
expecting `curl http://gateway/proxy/httpbin/get` to reach `https://httpbin.org/get` (as the equivalent TOML config does). Instead the full unstripped path is forwarded (`https://httpbin.org/proxy/httpbin/get`), which 404s against the real upstream. This is why `Ferrogate/Caddyfile` (the shipped default dev config) currently has no working httpbin-style proxy example — it's not possible to express one correctly in Caddyfile syntax today.

## Suggested fix
Add a `strip_prefix` (or Caddy-native `handle_path` semantics: `handle_path` implies stripping, plain `route`/`handle` does not) directive to the Caddyfile `route`/`handle`/`handle_path` parsing in `crates/ferrogate-config/src/caddyfile/parser.rs`, populating `GatewayRoute.strip_prefix` to match the TOML format's capability, then add a Caddyfile-format httpbin-proxy example back to `Ferrogate/Caddyfile` and README's Quick Start once it works.
title: [config][low] Caddyfile route blocks have no strip_prefix equivalent, unlike TOML's [[routes]]

**Severity: Low** · category: correctness · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
`billing.rs` (`ferrogate billing serve`) and `billing_client.rs` (the gateway's reporter) each hand-roll the same "inline value, else read + trim env var" token-resolution logic — and the two copies have **drifted**: `billing.rs`'s version trims the value read from the environment variable; `billing_client.rs`'s version does not.

## Failure scenario
An operator sources the gateway's billing bearer token from an environment variable populated via a mounted secret file (a common pattern, e.g. Kubernetes `envFrom`/`valueFrom` reading a file that ends in a trailing newline). `ferrogate billing serve --token-env FOO` trims it correctly (`billing.rs`), but the gateway's `BillingReporter::resolve_token` (`billing_client.rs:69`) returns the raw, untrimmed value and sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>\n` (or with trailing whitespace). `request_is_authorized` on the server side does a `strip_prefix("Bearer ")` + `.trim()` compare against the server's own (trimmed) token — the client's untrimmed value **never matches**, so every billing report from that gateway permanently 401s, with only a per-request warning log to notice it.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/billing.rs:40-60` — `resolve_token()`, trims the env-sourced token (`token.trim().to_string()`).
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/billing_client.rs:66-75` — `resolve_token()`, returns `std::env::var(env_name)` directly with no `.trim()`.

## Suggested fix
Trim the environment-sourced token in `billing_client.rs::resolve_token` to match `billing.rs`, or better: extract one shared `resolve_token(inline: Option<&str>, env_name: Option<&str>) -> anyhow::Result<Option<String>>` helper both call, so the two can't drift again.

**Severity: Medium** · category: correctness / schema · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
The gateway always stamps `occurred_at_unix: None` on the `BillingEvent` it forwards to the billing service. That `None` flows unmodified through the outbox → `deliver_once` → `POST /v1/billing/charge` → `ledger::charge()` (which copies it verbatim into `LedgerEntry.occurred_at_unix`) → `billing_ledger.occurred_at_unix` in Postgres. Every ledger row therefore has a **NULL** `occurred_at_unix`, making the `idx_billing_ledger_tenant_time(organization_id, project_id, occurred_at_unix)` index effectively useless for its primary purpose: time-scoped tenant queries/reporting.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4778` — `BillingEvent { ..., occurred_at_unix: None, ... }` set unconditionally in `record_billing_token_usage`.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/ledger.rs:151` — copies `event.occurred_at_unix` verbatim into `LedgerEntry`.
- `crates/ferrogate-storage/src/lib.rs:1377, 1412` — `append_billing_ledger_entry` persists it as-is.
- `sql/001_init_postgres.sql` — `idx_billing_ledger_tenant_time(organization_id, project_id, occurred_at_unix)`.

## Suggested fix
Stamp `occurred_at_unix` with the actual settlement time (e.g. `now_unix_seconds()`) in `record_billing_token_usage` instead of `None`, so ledger rows carry a real timestamp and the time-scoped tenant index is usable for reporting/reconciliation queries.

body:
**Severity: Medium** · category: design / defense-in-depth · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
Before the #135 fix, `charge()` unconditionally re-priced every event from the billing service's own `PriceBook`, so the standalone billing service acted as an **independent check** on the gateway's numbers. After #135, `authoritative_cost()` trusts *any* finite, non-negative `cost_usd` the gateway reports verbatim (only consulting the `PriceBook` for the input/output split ratio) — the billing service can no longer catch a gateway-side misconfiguration (e.g. a wrong price typo'd into `Model.input_price_per_1m`) as long as it produces a finite number.

This is a **known, intentional tradeoff** of #135 (single source of truth to stop the two systems silently diverging) — this issue is filed to make the reduced defense-in-depth trackable and propose a middle ground, not to suggest reverting #135.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/ledger.rs:156-160` — `authoritative_cost()`: `event.cost_usd.filter(|cost| cost.is_finite() && *cost >= 0.0)`.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/ledger.rs:109-132` — `charge()` honors that value with no comparison to what the `PriceBook` would have computed.

## Suggested fix
When both a gateway-settled `cost_usd` **and** a matching `PriceBook` entry exist, compute the `PriceBook` estimate anyway and log a warning (not an error — still honor the gateway's number per #135) when the two diverge beyond some tolerance. This preserves #135's single-source-of-truth guarantee while restoring visibility into gateway/billing-service rate-card drift, which is exactly the class of bug #135 itself was created to catch.

body:
**Severity: Medium** · category: reliability · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
`enqueue_billing_report`'s own failure (e.g. a transient DB blip while writing to the outbox) is only logged with `warn!` — nothing retries the enqueue itself, so a charge can still be **permanently lost** despite the "guaranteed delivery" design #137 introduced. This is a narrower window than the sweeper's delivery-retry-forever bug (see the companion issue), but it undermines the same durability claim: if the write that's supposed to make delivery durable fails, there's no second chance.

## Failure scenario
`record_billing_token_usage` (`state.rs:4805-4814`):
```rust
if let Err(error) = self.repositories.enqueue_billing_report(&entry_id, &event, now) {
    warn!(..., "failed to enqueue billing report for durable delivery");
}
```
If `enqueue_billing_report` returns `Err` (e.g. the Postgres pool is momentarily exhausted, a connection reset, a deadlock), the function logs a warning and returns `Ok(())` from `record_billing_token_usage` — the request completes normally, `append_billing_event` already succeeded (so local metering/rollups are correct), but the billing-service report is silently dropped forever. No retry, no fallback queue, no metric distinguishing this from a successful enqueue.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4805-4814` — the `if let Err(error) = ... { warn!(...) }` pattern, no retry or fallback.

## Suggested fix
At minimum, emit a distinguishable metric/counter for enqueue failures so operators can detect them (rather than only a log line). Consider a bounded in-process retry for the enqueue write itself, or accept the gap explicitly in documentation as a known narrow window (distinct from the sweeper's much bigger permanent-retry gap in the companion issue).

labels.description: Findings from an adversarial code review

title: [billing][medium] enqueue_billing_report failure is silently dropped with no retry of the enqueue itself

body:
**Severity: Medium** · category: efficiency · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
`record_billing_token_usage` now performs **two sequential, synchronous DB writes** in the request-response hot path for every billed request when billing reporting is enabled: `append_billing_event` (local metering/rollups) and then `enqueue_billing_report` (durable outbox for #137). Both block before the caller (`chat.rs`) can return the response to the client.

## Failure scenario
Every chat completion that extracts usage (`chat.rs:824, 1194, 1225`) synchronously calls into `record_billing_token_usage`, which does:
1. `self.repositories.append_billing_event(event.clone())` (`state.rs:4785`) — one blocking Postgres round-trip.
2. `self.repositories.enqueue_billing_report(&entry_id, &event, now)` (`state.rs:4808`) — a **second** blocking Postgres round-trip, only when `billing_reporter.is_some()`.

This is exactly the kind of hot-path DB write the outbox design was meant to keep off the request path (the sweeper, not the request, is supposed to own delivery latency) — but the *enqueue* itself is still synchronous and adds a full extra round-trip to response latency for every request, on top of the existing metering write.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4785` — `append_billing_event` (existing, pre-#137).
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4808` — `enqueue_billing_report` (new, synchronous, added for #137).
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/chat.rs:824, 1194, 1225` — call sites on the request-response path.

## Suggested fix
Combine the two writes into a single transaction (write the metering event and the outbox row together, since they're logically one commit), or move the outbox enqueue off the synchronous request path (e.g. buffer in memory and flush in a background task, accepting a small durability window), matching the "billing is a non-blocking accounting side effect" principle already established for reporter initialization (#139).

labels.name: code-review
labels.description: Findings from an adversarial code review

title: [billing][medium] record_billing_token_usage does two synchronous DB writes in the request hot path

body:
**Severity: Medium** · category: correctness / efficiency · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
`GET /v1/billing/ledger`'s per-tenant scoping (`organization_id`/`project_id`/`api_key_id`, added for #136) filters **after** global `offset`/`limit` pagination rather than pushing the predicate into the storage query. In a busy ledger, a tenant-scoped page can silently return **empty or incomplete** results, and the query never benefits from the existing `idx_billing_ledger_tenant_time` index.

## Failure scenario
`LedgerSink::list(offset, limit)` (`ledger.rs:199`) takes no tenant parameter; the Postgres implementation is `SELECT entry_json::text FROM billing_ledger ORDER BY created_at_unix ASC, id ASC OFFSET $1 LIMIT $2` (`lib.rs:1427-1432`) — global, unfiltered. `GET /v1/billing/ledger?organization_id=X` (`service.rs:188-202`) fetches **one page** this way (default limit 100, max 1000) and only then calls `filter_by_tenant` (`service.rs:283`) to narrow that one page in process.

If org `X`'s rows are not within the fetched oldest-first window (e.g. org `X` charges are newer than the default page, or sparse relative to a busy multi-tenant ledger), the caller gets an **empty `entries` array** and zero `page_totals` — indistinguishable from "no charges for this tenant" — even though rows exist further in the table. There is also no way to page *through* a tenant's full history without re-scanning and re-discarding every other tenant's rows for every page.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/ledger.rs:199` — `LedgerSink::list(offset, limit)` trait signature, no tenant parameter.
- `crates/ferrogate-storage/src/lib.rs:1427-1432` — the Postgres query, global order/offset/limit only.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs:188-202` — page-then-filter in the HTTP handler.
- `sql/001_init_postgres.sql` — `idx_billing_ledger_tenant_time(organization_id, project_id, occurred_at_unix)` exists but is unused by this query path.

## Suggested fix
Push the tenant filter into the storage query (`WHERE organization_id = $n AND project_id = $n ...`) so pagination operates on the already-scoped result set and can use `idx_billing_ledger_tenant_time`. Extend `LedgerSink::list` to accept an optional tenant filter, or add a dedicated `list_for_tenant` method.

**Severity: Medium** · category: closed-loop · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
`agent-worker --worker-type` (cloud vs self-hosted, added for #132) is wired to **exactly one** diagnostic subcommand (`WorkerType => print_worker_type`, which just emits a JSON evidence blob). None of the other 20+ real subcommands (`ServeManagementHttp`, `ServeManagementUnix`, the `Governed*ExecutionSmoke` family, etc.) take `cli.worker_type` as a parameter at all — every actual execution path hardcodes `FrameworkAdapterMode::Managed`.

## Failure scenario
An operator reads #132's resolution ("one shared binary + `--worker-type cloud|self-hosted` mapping to `FrameworkAdapterMode`") and reasonably expects `agent-worker --worker-type self-hosted serve-management-http ...` to actually run in self-hosted (report-only, non-enforced) mode. It doesn't — the flag is accepted by clap but silently ignored by every subcommand except the diagnostic print, so the process behaves identically to cloud/managed mode regardless of the flag.

## Evidence
- `crates/agent-worker/src/main.rs:92-93` — `cli.worker_type: WorkerType` declared as a global clap arg.
- `crates/agent-worker/src/main.rs:287` — `Command::WorkerType => print_worker_type(cli.worker_type)` is the only consumer.
- `crates/agent-worker/src/main.rs:286-394` — every other subcommand match arm constructs its session/runtime without referencing `cli.worker_type` at all, hardcoding the managed path.

## Suggested fix
Either thread `cli.worker_type` into the actual session/runtime construction for the subcommands that matter (at minimum `ServeManagementHttp`/`ServeManagementUnix`, mapping to `FrameworkAdapterMode`), or — if self-hosted execution genuinely isn't implemented yet — say so explicitly in `--help`/docs and reject `--worker-type self-hosted` on subcommands that don't support it, rather than silently accepting and ignoring it. This was flagged as a deferred scope item when #132 was closed; this issue makes that gap trackable on its own.

## Summary
`crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs` hand-rolls a **second, near-identical copy** of `ferrogate-auth`'s HTTP/1.1 server (`HttpRequest`/`HttpResponse`/`read_http_request`/`find_header_end`). The #138 hardening (per-connection read/write timeouts, connection-count cap, `Content-Length` overflow guard) landed **only in the new billing copy** — `ferrogate-auth`'s `serve()` (unchanged by this diff) still has none of it and remains exposed to the same slowloris / thread-exhaustion / overflow issues #138 fixed for billing.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs:39-46` — `CONNECTION_TIMEOUT`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS` (the #138 fix).
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs:143-152` — `handle_connection` sets `set_read_timeout`/`set_write_timeout`.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs:381-389` — `read_http_request` bounds `Content-Length` with `checked_add` before indexing.
- `crates/ferrogate-auth/src/lib.rs:415-421, 489-548` — the near-identical, **unhardened** original: `handle_connection` never sets a read/write timeout, the accept loop spawns one thread per connection with no cap, and `content_length` is used to index the body buffer without an overflow check.

## Failure scenario
A client opens a connection to `ferrogate auth serve` and sends a partial request, then goes idle — the handler thread blocks forever (no read timeout), exactly the slowloris pattern #138 fixed for billing. A malformed huge `Content-Length` header against the auth service can overflow/panic the same way the billing service did before #138.

## Suggested fix
Extract the hardened HTTP/1.1 helper (timeouts, connection cap, bounded `Content-Length` parsing, request/response types) into a small shared internal crate or module both `ferrogate-auth` and `ferrogate-billing` depend on, and port `ferrogate-auth`'s `serve()` onto it. This also prevents the two implementations drifting further apart on future hardening.

body:
**Severity: High** · category: closed-loop / correctness · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
Monthly-budget enforcement and the standalone billing ledger are **two independent, silently-divergent cost sources**, and only the (possibly wrong/zero) gateway-side number gates spend. The billing ledger's own — potentially correct — price is never fed back into enforcement.

## Failure scenario
Configure a model on a route with **no** `input_price_per_1m`/`output_price_per_1m` (exactly the pattern the shipped `config/ferrogate.token4ai.example.toml` shows for several commented-out vendor blocks, e.g. Anthropic/Gemini/Grok), while `ferrogate billing serve` runs with its **default rate card** (`crates/ferrogate-billing/src/pricing.rs:147-166`), which *does* price that model.

For every request on that route:
1. `settled_cost_usd()` returns `None` (no route price) → `BillingEvent.cost_usd = None`.
2. `usage_monthly_rollups.cost_usd` — the number `monthly_budget_exceeded` (`state.rs:4465-4490`) reads to gate further spend — accumulates `0` for these requests (see `append_billing_event` → `increment_usage_monthly_rollups`).
3. The event is still enqueued to the billing outbox; the billing service (no `cost_usd` present) re-prices it from its own `PriceBook` and correctly records a nonzero charge in `billing_ledger`.

Net effect: the operator has a real, correctly-priced dollar figure sitting in `billing_ledger`, while the enforcement path that's supposed to stop overspend sees `$0` for the same requests and **never trips**. The two "parallel cost stores" don't just duplicate work — they diverge, and the wrong one is load-bearing for spend control.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:6828-6845` — `settled_cost_usd` returns `None` when route prices are absent.
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4465-4490` — `monthly_budget_exceeded` reads only `usage_monthly_rollups.cost_usd`.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/pricing.rs:147-166` — the billing service's independent default rate card, which can price a model the gateway route config does not.
- `config/ferrogate.token4ai.example.toml` — ships exactly this configuration shape (commented models with no price fields, alongside `[billing_service]` enabled).

## Suggested fix
Either (a) have the gateway read the settled `LedgerEntry.cost` back from the billing service (synchronously or via a periodic sync) and feed it into `usage_monthly_rollups`, or (b) refuse to enable `billing_service` for a route that has no gateway-side price configured (fail closed at config-validation time, consistent with the project's fail-closed conventions), or (c) make the billing service's `PriceBook` the single source both budget enforcement and the ledger read from. Cross-reference #135 (which addressed the *reverse* direction: gateway price should win over the billing service's price) — this finding is the mirror case where the gateway has *no* price at all.

body:
**Severity: High** · category: correctness · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128) — independently verified beyond the reviewer's "plausible" vote

## Summary
The gateway's own cost settlement (`settled_cost_usd`, which produces the *authoritative* `BillingEvent.cost_usd` honored verbatim by the billing ledger per #135) **never reconciles a missing prompt/completion split** before pricing. `TokenUsage::reconcile_split()` — added specifically to fix this class of bug for issue #140 — is wired only into `ferrogate_billing::ledger::charge()`'s independent-PriceBook fallback path, **not** into the gateway's own settlement path, which takes precedence whenever the gateway has a route price configured (the common production case).

## Failure scenario
A provider adapter returns usage as `{"total_tokens": 1000}` with no `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` (exactly the scenario `reconcile_split`'s own doc comment names: "some providers report only a total, or omit one side of the split"). In `record_billing_token_usage`:
1. `estimate_missing_total()` is called (`state.rs:4754`) — a no-op here since `total_tokens` is already nonzero (it only fills a *missing total* from the split, not the reverse).
2. `settled_cost_usd()` (`state.rs:6828-6845`) computes `ModelPrice::estimate(usage)` directly on `prompt_tokens=0, completion_tokens=0` → `input_cost=0, output_cost=0, total_cost=0.0`.
3. The resulting `BillingEvent.cost_usd = Some(0.0)`.
4. In `ledger.rs`, `authoritative_cost()` filters `cost.is_finite() && *cost >= 0.0` — **`0.0` passes.** `charge()` therefore honors it as `CostSource::GatewaySettled` with `total_cost = 0.0`.

Result: the billing ledger **permanently records a $0 charge** for a real, token-consuming request. This is precisely the failure mode #140 was meant to close — but the fix landed on the wrong (lower-precedence) code path.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4754` — `draft.usage.clone().estimate_missing_total()` (not `reconcile_split()`).
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:6828-6845` — `settled_cost_usd` prices `usage.prompt_tokens`/`usage.completion_tokens` directly, no split reconciliation.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/ledger.rs:110` — `reconcile_split()` is called only inside `charge()`, which is only reached for the `PriceBook` estimate — the `authoritative_cost` branch bypasses the `usage` variable's derivation before `settled_breakdown` computes a scaled split from an *already-wrong* zero-cost total.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/lib.rs:64` — `reconcile_split()` definition, confirming its intended scope ("before pricing").

## Suggested fix
Call `reconcile_split()` (or equivalent) on `usage` in `record_billing_token_usage` **before** `settled_cost_usd()` is invoked, so the gateway's own settlement sees the same reconciled split the billing-service fallback already does. Add a test where usage is `(0, 0, N)` and assert `settled_cost_usd` returns a positive amount, not `Some(0.0)`.

body:
**Severity: High** · category: closed-loop / reliability · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
The billing-outbox sweeper thread is spawned **exactly once at gateway boot**, gated on whether billing reporting is enabled in the *startup* config snapshot. Enabling `billing_service` later via the supported hot config-reload path never starts a drain thread — the outbox will accept enqueues but nothing ever delivers them until the process is restarted.

## Failure scenario
Start `ferrogate gateway` with `billing_service.enabled = false` (the default). `serve()` calls `start_billing_outbox_sweeper(&state)` once (`gateway/mod.rs:170`), which checks `state.current().billing_reporting_enabled()` and returns `None` (no thread) since it's false at boot. An operator later flips `billing_service.enabled = true` and triggers the gateway's supported in-process admin config-reload. The reload swaps `AppState`'s config (and rebuilds `billing_reporter`), but no code path re-evaluates whether a sweeper thread needs to start — the one-time boot-time decision is never revisited.

Every request from that point onward correctly enqueues into `billing_report_outbox` (the write path checks the *current* `billing_reporter`), but the reports sit there undelivered indefinitely, silently, with no error surfaced.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/mod.rs:170` — `start_billing_outbox_sweeper(&state)` called once in `serve()`, before `run_forever()`.
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/gateway/mod.rs:351` — the sweeper's existence check (`billing_reporting_enabled()`) is evaluated only at that one call site.
- Admin config-reload path swaps the config/state without touching the sweeper handle.

## Suggested fix
Either (a) always spawn the sweeper thread and have it no-op (or check `billing_reporting_enabled()` on every tick) rather than being enabled only if billing was on at boot, or (b) hook the admin config-reload path to start/stop the sweeper when `billing_service.enabled` changes. Add a test that enables billing via reload (not boot config) and asserts a report is delivered.

body:
**Severity: High** · category: closed-loop / reliability · from a follow-up xhigh code review of the merged billing/service-decomposition work (epic #128)

## Summary
The durable billing outbox (added for #137) **retries a permanently-failing delivery forever**, with no max-attempts or dead-letter state. This regresses a guarantee the old fire-and-forget `BillingReporter::report()` actually had: it capped retries at `MAX_REPORT_ATTEMPTS = 3` and then gave up.

## Failure scenario
A request is priced with no gateway-settled cost (`cost_usd = None`) and the billing service's own `PriceBook` has no rule for `(provider, provider_model)` — a realistic drift whenever an operator adds a model to the gateway's route config without a matching rate-card entry in the separately-configured billing service. `charge()` returns `price_not_found` → HTTP 422 (a **permanent** client/config error, not transient).

`sweep_billing_outbox_once` (`state.rs:4843-4881`) treats this identically to a transient network failure: on any `Err` from `deliver_once` it always calls `billing_outbox_backoff_secs(entry.attempts)` (`state.rs:7716-7723`, capped at 60s) and reschedules — never deletes, never marks terminal. `metering::post_json` treats any non-2xx as `Err`, so a 422 is indistinguishable from a 5xx to the sweeper.

Consequence: that one outbox row retries roughly every 60s **forever**. `list_due_billing_reports` batches 100 rows ordered by `next_attempt_unix ASC`, so enough poison rows can starve delivery of newer, actually-deliverable reports. There is no CLI/admin surface to inspect or purge stuck rows, and no test exercises this path.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4843-4881` — `sweep_billing_outbox_once`, unconditional reschedule on any error.
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:7716-7723` — `billing_outbox_backoff_secs`, caps interval only, never stops.
- `crates/ferrogate-storage/src/lib.rs` — `reschedule_billing_report` (Postgres + in-memory) only increments `attempts`/`next_attempt_unix`, never deletes.
- `sql/001_init_postgres.sql` — `billing_report_outbox` has no TTL/max-attempts/dead-letter column.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/ledger.rs` — `charge()` fails closed with `price_not_found` when no cost is available.

## Suggested fix
Cap attempts (e.g. after N attempts or a wall-clock age) and move the row to a terminal/dead-letter state (or a separate `billing_report_dead_letters` table) instead of retrying indefinitely. Distinguish permanent errors (4xx from the billing service) from transient ones (network/5xx) so a 422 doesn't retry at all. Add an admin/CLI surface to list and purge dead-lettered reports, and a test exercising the give-up path.

**Severity: Medium** · category: correctness (under-billing) · from the code review of the service-decomposition branch (epic #128)

## Summary
Cost is computed **only** from `prompt_tokens` + `completion_tokens`. A usage record that reports its output count only in `total_tokens` (with `completion_tokens` absent/0) is billed with **$0 output** — under-billing every such request.

## Failure scenario
A Gemini response returns `usageMetadata` with `promptTokenCount` and `totalTokenCount` but omits `candidatesTokenCount`, so `extract_usage` yields `prompt=Some(P), completion=None, total=Some(T)` (`gemini.rs:133-148`). `record_billing_event` maps the missing split to 0 (`state.rs:4707-4711`), producing `prompt=P, completion=0, total=T`.

`charge()` calls `estimate_missing_total()` (`ledger.rs:88`), but that only fills a **zero total from the split** — it never derives a missing split side from a non-zero total (`lib.rs:49-56`). `ModelPrice::estimate` then prices only `prompt_tokens` and `completion_tokens` (`lib.rs:73-86`), so the `T - P` output tokens are billed at **$0**.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/lib.rs:49-56` (`estimate_missing_total`), `lib.rs:73-86` (`ModelPrice::estimate` ignores `total_tokens`).
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/ledger.rs:88` — `charge()` relies on `estimate_missing_total`.
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4707-4711` — missing split mapped to 0.

## Suggested fix
When `completion_tokens == 0` but `total_tokens > prompt_tokens`, derive `completion_tokens = total_tokens - prompt_tokens` (and symmetrically for a missing prompt side) before pricing — or reject/flag usage records whose split does not reconcile with `total_tokens` rather than billing the missing side at $0.

body:
**Severity: Medium** · category: robustness / security (DoS) · from the code review of the service-decomposition branch (epic #128)

The billing service's hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 server (`crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs`) has two robustness defects. Both are reachable pre-auth (see #136).

## 1. Slowloris / thread exhaustion (no read timeout, unbounded threads)
`serve()` spawns **one OS thread per accepted connection with no cap**, and `read_http_request` loops on `stream.read()` until it sees `\r\n\r\n`. The accepted `TcpStream` never gets `set_read_timeout`/`set_write_timeout`, so a client that connects and sends a partial request (`GET /healthz HTTP/1.1\r\n` then nothing) parks its handler thread **forever**. A few thousand idle connections exhaust threads/memory and block legitimate charge reports.
- Evidence: `service.rs:89-101` (unbounded `thread::spawn` per accept), `service.rs:215-230` (blocking read loop, no timeout set).
- Fix: set read/write timeouts on each accepted stream immediately; bound concurrent connection threads (worker pool / semaphore); optionally rate-limit the charge endpoint.

## 2. Content-Length overflow panic
`content_length` is parsed **unbounded** (`service.rs:249-253`); the `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` guard only bounds `buffer.len()`, never `content_length`. Then `buffer[body_start..body_start + content_length]` (`service.rs:273`) overflows: debug builds panic on the add (`attempt to add with overflow`); release builds wrap to `start > end` and panic on the slice.
- Failure input: `POST /v1/billing/charge` with `Content-Length: 18446744073709551615` and a tiny body → handler thread panics.
- Fix: reject (400/413) when `content_length > MAX_REQUEST_BYTES`; compute the end with `body_start.checked_add(content_length)`.

## Note
The same hand-rolled server shape is shared with `ferrogate-auth` (`lib.rs`), which has the same missing read-timeout; consider factoring a small hardened HTTP helper both services use.

body:
**Severity: Medium** · category: reliability / durability · from the code review of the service-decomposition branch (epic #128)

## Summary
The gateway→billing usage report is **fire-and-forget with no retry, queue, or reconciliation**, so settled charges are silently lost whenever the billing service is unavailable or rejects the event — desynchronizing `billing_ledger` from the gateway's `usage_monthly_rollups`.

## Failure scenarios
1. **Billing down / network partition / 5xx.** For every settled request, `record_billing_token_usage → reporter.report(event)` posts to `/v1/billing/charge`; on error `report()` emits a single `tracing::warn!` and drops the event. No retry, no outbox, no reconciliation. The gateway keeps serving, but those charges never reach the ledger.
2. **Unknown model → 422.** If the billing `PriceBook` has no entry for a model the gateway *does* price and budget (the default card has **no `("*","*")` catch-all**), `charge()` returns `price_not_found` → HTTP 422 → the reporter drops it. The gateway metered and budgeted the request, but the ledger records nothing → **systematic under-count**.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/billing_client.rs:51-79` — `report()` warns-and-drops on failure; no retry/queue.
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4794` — sole fire-and-forget call site.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs:173-184` — 422 on `price_not_found`; `metering.rs` bails on non-2xx.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/pricing.rs:147-167` — default rate card has no `("*","*")` fallback.
- Secondary (perf): `billing_client.rs:53` uses an **unbounded** `spawn_blocking` per request with a fresh TCP connect and no concurrency cap — a slow billing dependency can back up the shared Tokio blocking pool (also used by metering/streaming). Bound in-flight reports with a semaphore or a single drain task.

## Suggested fix
- Since `BillingEvent`s are already persisted (`state.rs:4774`), add a background sweeper that re-POSTs un-acked events to `/v1/billing/charge` (idempotent on `ledger_entry_id`, so replay is double-bill-safe), **or** make `report()` write to a bounded persistent outbox with retry/backoff instead of warn-and-drop.
- Give the billing service a configurable `("*","*")` fallback, or make a missing price a hard config/startup error rather than a per-request silent drop.
- Add a reconciliation check that ledger totals match `usage_monthly_rollups.cost_usd` for a period.

body:
**Severity: High** · category: security / authentication · from the code review of the service-decomposition branch (epic #128)

## Summary
The billing service authenticates **no one**. `route_request` dispatches purely on `(method, path)` and `read_http_request` never parses an `Authorization` header. The gateway client is built to send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (`billing_client.rs` `resolve_token`; `metering.rs:331`), and the config documents `token`/`token_env` as the "service-to-service bearer token" — but the server discards it, giving a **false sense of protection**.

## Failure scenario
Any process that can reach the billing port (default `127.0.0.1:8092`, but the bind address is operator-controlled and commonly `0.0.0.0` for a decomposed microservice) can:
1. `POST /v1/billing/charge` with a hand-crafted `BillingEvent` (`tenant.api_key_id` = a victim, `usage.total_tokens = 1_000_000_000`) → the service prices and persists it → **forged charges / ledger poisoning against any tenant**.
2. `GET /v1/billing/ledger?limit=1000` → exfiltrate every tenant's `request_id`, `trace_id`, model, usage, cost, credits → **cross-tenant billing-data disclosure**.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs:113-158` — `route_request` matches only `(method, path)`; charge arm has no caller check.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs:215-275` — `read_http_request` parses method/path/query/content-length only; no `Authorization`.
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/service.rs:40-45` — `BillingServiceConfig` has no server-secret field; `BillingServeArgs` (`cli.rs`) exposes no server token flag.
- Contrast client side: `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/billing_client.rs` resolves a bearer token; `metering.rs:331` emits it.

## Suggested fix
- Add a `token` field to `ferrogate_billing::BillingServiceConfig` and a `--token`/`--token-env` flag to `ferrogate billing serve`.
- Parse the `Authorization` header in `read_http_request`; in `route_request`, reject charge/ledger requests whose bearer token does not **constant-time-match** the configured secret (401 on mismatch/absence).
- Scope `GET /v1/billing/ledger` to the authenticated caller's tenant instead of exposing the global ledger.
- Add an E2E asserting an unauthenticated request is rejected.

body:
**Severity: High** · category: correctness / data-integrity · from the code review of the service-decomposition branch (epic #128)

## Summary
The billing ledger and the gateway hot path price the **same request from two independent rate cards** and persist two different "cost" numbers that silently diverge.

After the P1-4 rebase, the gateway settles cost on the hot path from the **config** `Model.input_price_per_1m/output_price_per_1m` (`settled_cost_usd`, `state.rs:6758-6776`), stores it on `BillingEvent.cost_usd`, increments `usage_monthly_rollups.cost_usd`, and **enforces the monthly budget** against that number. It then forwards the same event (carrying `cost_usd`) to the billing service, whose `charge()` **ignores `event.cost_usd`** and re-prices from its own `PriceBook` (`ledger.rs:74-90`). `StorageLedgerSink` writes that PriceBook cost into `billing_ledger.total_cost`.

## Failure scenario
Config prices gpt-5.5 at 2.0/6.0 per 1M (a negotiated rate). Gateway settles a 1M-in/1M-out request at **$8.00**, budgets against $8.00. The billing service, started without `--pricing`, uses `with_default_rate_card()` (5.0/15.0) and records **$20.00** in `billing_ledger` — a 2.5× divergence between the enforced cost and the "settled money flow" ledger. The two are never reconciled and live in unlinked tables.

## Evidence
- `crates/ferrogate-billing/src/ledger.rs:74-90` — `charge()` calls `book.price_for(&event.provider, &event.provider_model)`; never reads `event.cost_usd`.
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/state.rs:4746-4776` — gateway settles `cost_usd` from config, persists to metering/rollups, then reports the event at `state.rs:4794`.
- `crates/ferrogate-cli/src/billing.rs:38-47` — PriceBook comes only from `--pricing` or the default card, with no link to the gateway model registry.
- The E2E only asserts `cost > 0` (`tools/ferrogate-test/src/scenarios.rs`), so the divergence is invisible in tests.

## Suggested fix
Pick a single pricing authority:
- **Preferred:** `charge()` honors `event.cost_usd` when `Some` (only re-prices when `None`), so the ledger equals the budget-enforced cost; or
- feed the billing service the same rate table the gateway uses; or
- drop one of the two cost computations.
Then strengthen the E2E to assert `ledger.cost == gateway-settled cost` for a model whose config price differs from the default card.

## 背景

当前代码已经是细粒度的 crate 模块化拆分（`ferrogate-billing` / `ferrogate-auth` / `ferrogate-providers` / `agent-worker` 等），但**运行时固化到服务器上的二进制入口**还没有拆分成一组相互调用的独立服务进程。目前的二进制：

- `ferrogate`（`crates/ferrogate-cli`）—— 网关 + 子命令（`Run` / `Auth` / `Storage` / `Validate` / `Reload` / `HashKey`）
- `ferrogate-auth`（独立 bin）
- `agent-worker`（独立 bin）
- `ferrogate-test`（`tools/ferrogate-test`，E2E 测试脚手架）

`ferrogate-billing` 目前只是一个**计量库**（`TokenUsage`），还不是一个能把 usage 计费成金额/额度流水的独立微服务。

## 目标

把运行时拆分成一组**独立进程**，通过**单一 `ferrogate` 二进制的子命令**分别启动，进程之间通过 **REST / HTTP** 互相调用，整条链路端到端跑通，并用 `ferrogate-test` 打透到 Supabase Postgres。

```
ferrogate
  ├── gateway     # agentic AI 网关
  ├── auth        # 登录/注册 + org/workspace/tenant + RBAC + 虚拟 API Key
  └── billing     # 把网关传来的 usage token 计费成金额/额度流水

ferrogate-test    # E2E 测试脚手架，覆盖打透到 Supabase PG
  └── agent-worker # 云端托管 runtime / 自托管 worker 进程
```

## 验收标准（整体）

- [ ] 单一 `ferrogate` 二进制，可通过子命令独立启动 `gateway` / `auth` / `billing` 三个服务进程

- [ ] `billing` 服务：**只传 usage token 即可拿到对应的计费流水**（金额消耗 or 额度消耗），参考 sub2api 的计费实现
- [ ] `agent-worker` 云端托管 vs 自托管两种 worker 类型的二进制命名方案确定并落地（详见子 issue）
- [ ] 网关能服务 **gpt-5.5** 上游模型调用，配置上游 `https://api.token4ai.cloud/v1` + api-key

Epic: [TOK-10](mention://issue/93cd4f44-c4d4-412c-a419-6b3ab3d242a5) · Phase 1 · Stage 4（依赖 P1-2/P1-3）

## 目标

用量与成本统计：按 key / workspace / project / tenant 四维度聚合 token、cost、latency、status，并提供报表查询 API，为 P1-3 月预算提供累计数据源。

## 现状

- `ferrogate-billing`：已有 `TokenUsage` / `ModelPrice` / `CostEstimate` / `BillingEvent` + `InMemoryBillingEventSink`（`crates/ferrogate-billing/src/lib.rs`）—— 有成本估算，无持久化聚合、无多维度报表。
- SQL 已有 `metering_events` / `usage_aggregates` / `usage_aggregate_rollups`（`sql/001_init_postgres.sql`）—— 需接上四层归属维度。

## 交付

1. **落账**：每次请求记录 `tenant_id, project_id, workspace_id, api_key_id, provider, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, cost_usd, latency_ms, status`。复用/扩展 `metering_events`，补齐四维度列（若缺）。
2. **聚合**：按 (维度, 时间窗如日/月) 汇总 token/cost/请求数/错误数，写入 `usage_aggregates`。为月预算提供「本月某 scope 累计 cost」的快速查询。
3. **报表 API**：按 tenant/project/workspace/key + 时间范围查询用量与成本；支持 group by 维度。
4. **接线**：把 P1-3 的「读月度累计」接到本 stage 的聚合查询，闭环月预算。
5. **测试**：四维度落账、聚合正确、月累计查询、报表分组。

## 约束

- 落账不阻塞请求主路径（异步/批量 sink，参考现有 billing sink 抽象）。
- `cargo test` + `clippy` 通过。

完成后 Phase 1 主体闭环：签发 key → 绑定 workspace → 请求鉴权 → 配额校验 → 四维度用量/成本落账。

## 数据库规范约束（用户澄清 2026-07-03）

所有 Phase 1 控制面持久化都必须使用 Supabase（PostgreSQL wire / `storage.provider = supabase`）。不得为本 Epic 新增 MySQL 或 libSQL 持久化表、迁移或运行时读写路径；memory 仅限测试/降级。

## 持久化约束（Supabase 系统级要求 · 用户新增）

本环节所有新增/变更的控制面资源 **必须落地到 Supabase 的真实表中持久化**，不允许停留在 YAML / 内存 / 进程态：

- 新增表进入 `sql/001_init_postgres.sql`（Supabase 跑的就是这份 PostgreSQL schema），并 bump `POSTGRES_SCHEMA_VERSION` / schema name；不得同步 MySQL/libSQL schema。
- 读写一律走 `ferrogate-storage` 的 durable 后端（`storage.provider = supabase`，PostgreSQL wire）；in-memory 仅作为测试/降级路径，不得作为唯一真相源。
- 集成测试至少覆盖 Postgres/Supabase 后端一条端到端读写路径（可用本地 Postgres 兼容 Supabase schema），验证数据真正落表并可回读。

## 目标

## 交付

2. **解析规则**：请求解析出归属链后，从 key→workspace→project→tenant 逐层合并策略：**就近覆盖生效值，上层作为封顶**（下层不得突破上层限额）。模型白名单取交集。
3. **限流实现**：RPM/TPM 滑动/固定窗口计数（先用进程内 + 可选 Redis 抽象，MVP 进程内即可，留 trait 供集群扩展）。月预算基于 P1-4 的用量累计（本 stage 先做「读累计 + 超限拒绝」的接口，累计落账在 P1-4）。
4. **热路径校验**：在网关请求入口做 fail-closed 校验：key 禁用/过期、模型不在白名单、超 RPM/TPM、超月预算 → 拒绝并返回结构化错误（参考现有 `invalid_api_key` 错误风格，`crates/ferrogate-auth/src/lib.rs:255`）。
5. **测试**：多层级覆盖与封顶、白名单交集、RPM/TPM 触发、预算超限拒绝、fail-closed。

## 约束

- 配额缺失 = 不限制（除非上层设了封顶）；但认证失败/系统错误 = fail-closed 拒绝。

Multica issue: TOK-12

Implement Virtual API Key management for the Phase 1 AI Gateway control plane.

Scope:

- Add durable `api_keys` storage in Supabase/PostgreSQL only.
- Bind keys to `workspace_id` and store redundant `tenant_id/project_id` for routing, quota, metering, and audit attribution.
- Generate `fg_` keys and return plaintext only on create/rotate.
- Store only `key_hash`, `key_prefix`, and `last4`, never plaintext secrets.

## Closed-loop gap: no Supabase edge-functions entry for tools/functions

**Severity:** fatal for the stated end-to-end loop (completeness)

The intended closed loop is: AI gateway → MCP servers/tools → **functions invoked through a Supabase edge-functions entry** → agent worker (cloud-managed + self-hosted), with full-link management & security.

Repo-wide audit finds **no Supabase edge-functions integration**:
- No `supabase/functions/` directory, no `*.ts`/Deno function sources.
- No Rust code invoking a Supabase edge function (`functions/v1`, edge-function client, service/anon-key invocation) — `grep -rin edge --include=*.rs` over `crates/` and `tools/` returns nothing.
- The closest surrogate is a generic governed REST action (`crates/ferrogate-runtime/src/managed_external_action.rs` `ManagedExternalAction::Rest`, executed by `agent-worker/src/external_actions.rs::execute_governed_rest_action`), which is not a dedicated edge-functions entry (no Supabase function routing, no Supabase auth/JWT, no per-tenant function registry).

### Impact
The "functions via Supabase edge functions" link of the loop is unimplemented, so the end-to-end chain is not closed at this hop. Governance/records exist for external actions, but there is no first-class path to invoke serverless functions through Supabase edge functions.

### Ask
Design + implement the Supabase edge-functions invocation entry: function registry/config, invocation client (endpoint + auth), capability/policy governance reusing the external-action boundary, and an end-to-end scenario in `ferrogate-test` that drives gateway → edge function → agent worker. Track as an epic if it needs to be split.
title: Closed-loop gap: Supabase edge-functions entry for tools/functions is unimplemented

body:
## Non-constant-time comparison of self-hosted worker bearer secret (timing side-channel)

**Severity:** high (hardening on the auth path)

`crates/ferrogate-runtime/src/self_hosted_worker.rs:140`:

```rust
if worker.token_id != identity.token_id || worker.token_secret != identity.token_secret {
    return Err(SelfHostedWorkerError::InvalidIdentity(...));
}
```

`token_secret` is a bearer secret authenticating a self-hosted worker. Comparing it with `String`/`&str` `!=` short-circuits on the first differing byte, leaking secret-prefix length via response timing to an attacker who can submit many identity attempts.

### Fix
Compare `token_secret` in constant time (e.g. `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` — `subtle` is already in the tree transitively via `chacha20poly1305`). Keep `token_id` as a normal lookup key; only the secret needs constant-time equality. Add a test asserting a wrong secret of equal length is rejected.
title: Self-hosted worker token secret compared in non-constant time (timing side-channel)

body:
## Fatal: self-hosted worker identity-expiry can be bypassed with client-controlled time

**Severity:** fatal (authentication bypass)

`SelfHostedWorkerRegistry::validate_identity` enforces token expiry by comparing `identity.observed_at_unix` against the registered `identity_expires_at_unix`:

```rust
// crates/ferrogate-runtime/src/self_hosted_worker.rs:145-153
if worker
    .identity_expires_at_unix
    .zip(identity.observed_at_unix)
    .is_some_and(|(expires_at, observed_at)| observed_at >= expires_at)
{ return Err(... "worker identity has expired" ...); }
```

`observed_at_unix` is **client-controlled** — `SelfHostedRunPollRequest` (and the identity envelope) are deserialized directly from the worker's request body (`gateway/local.rs:4416 read_self_hosted_transport_body::<SelfHostedRunPollRequest>`). The two server-side enforcement wrappers only stamp the server clock when the field is **absent**:

- `state.rs:2712` — `if observed_identity.observed_at_unix.is_none() { … = now_unix_seconds(); }`
- `state.rs:5247` — `if request.identity.observed_at_unix.is_none() { … = Some(request.now_unix); }` (and `request.now_unix` is itself client-supplied)

### Exploit
A self-hosted worker holding an **expired** (or since-expiry-revoked) token sends `observed_at_unix = Some(0)`. The `is_none()` guard is false, so the server keeps the client value; `0 >= expires_at` is false → not expired → identity accepted. The worker can register/heartbeat/poll run dispatches **indefinitely** past expiry. On the poll path the check runs entirely on attacker time (`request.now_unix` also client-controlled).

### Fix
Never trust client time for expiry. In both wrappers, **unconditionally overwrite** `observed_at_unix` with `now_unix_seconds()` (server clock), ignoring any client-supplied value. Add regression tests: an expired token with client `observed_at_unix = Some(0)` must be rejected.
title: Fatal: self-hosted worker identity-expiry bypass (client-controlled observed_at_unix)

- Investigate and fix the `ferrogate-cli --test ai_proxy_runtime` case that fails only under `cargo llvm-cov` instrumentation (timing sensitivity in the report run).


## Control-plane → Supabase penetration (控制面打透到 supabase db)
This module writes/reads durable control-plane state. Scenarios MUST drive a **real Supabase/Postgres** instance (Docker `postgres`/`supabase-provider-local`), not the in-memory repository, and assert the rows actually landed in the DB. Verify migrations, upserts, idempotency, tenant scoping, and read-back consistency end to end.


## Cross-cutting requirements
- **Scenario-based**: cover every business-relevant facet of this module (happy path, each failure mode, boundary/edge inputs, and adversarial/tamper cases), not just isolated unit fragments.
- **Full-link (全链路)**: exercise the real operator entrypoint → gateway/worker execution → observable evidence, not mocked-in-isolation fragments.
- **Framework**: use the shared open-source stack — `rstest` (fixtures + parametrized cases), `proptest` (invariants/property tests), and the repo `ferrogate-test` harness for Docker-backed E2E.
- **Report-driven**: run `cargo llvm-cov` for this module, attach the before/after coverage, and fix every defect the scenarios surface (`将产出的测试报告针对性的修复`).

## Definition of done
- New scenario cases live in a dedicated `*_test.rs` / `tests/` target (not inline in business-logic files).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, and the new tests pass.
- Coverage for the module measurably increases; defects found are fixed in the same slice.

## Problem

`tools/ferrogate-test/src/main.rs` has grown into a large monolithic test harness. `main.rs` should stay close to the CLI entrypoint and orchestration layer, not contain most scenario-specific business logic, mock servers, HTTP helpers, Docker scenarios, and assertion code.

Refactor incrementally by business/testing surface, keeping behavior locked by existing local harness commands before moving code.

- `cli`: clap command definitions and top-level dispatch.
- `local`: local gateway harness lifecycle and shared HTTP assertion helpers.
- `scenarios::admin`, `scenarios::auth`, `scenarios::gateway`, `scenarios::storage`, `scenarios::docker`: scenario entrypoints.
- `mocks`: provider, billing, OTLP, MCP/agent, auth mock servers.
- `fixtures`: local config generation, certificates, static JSON fixtures.
- `assertions`: JSONL, redaction, OTLP trace/log/metric assertions, API response assertions.

## Constraints

- No behavior change in the first split.
- No new dependencies unless there is a concrete reduction in complexity.
- Keep `ferrogate-test ci`, `gateway-api`, `admin-api`, and Docker-backed scenarios working through the same CLI contract.
- Move one module boundary at a time and verify with local commands.

## Acceptance criteria

- `main.rs` only contains attribution printing, CLI parsing, and dispatch into modules.

- Mock servers and shared assertions are not mixed into scenario bodies.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p ferrogate-test --locked`, and focused `ferrogate-test` scenarios pass after each slice.

Related context: this follows the repo rule that entrypoints should expose a highly abstracted call chain instead of carrying large business logic directly.
